# Swarm networking surface area

Scope: Swarm networking: the configuration of the cluster and its nodes, Swarm-scoped networks, the
overlay network driver's options and networks, and the ingress network, as observable from outside
the daemon.

This document is a behavior specification. For how the parts work, see [design.md](../../../daemon/libnetwork/docs/design.md), [network.md](../../../daemon/libnetwork/docs/network.md) and [networkdb.md](../../../daemon/libnetwork/docs/networkdb.md).

[../README.md](../README.md) gives the model that this spec follows: the items of a spec, their
categories and what their verdicts depend on. [README.md](README.md) gives the conventions of the
networking specs, such as vantage points, daemon settings, timing and convergence ceilings, and host
requirements. The other specs in this directory use the same conventions. Unless an expectation says
otherwise, a `ctr` in this document is a standalone container attached to an `attachable`
overlay.

In this spec, an overlay network is an overlay network other than the ingress network, unless an
expectation includes the ingress network. A node has a local attachment to a network while a task, a
standalone container or the node's load-balancer endpoint on that network is on the node. A network
is programmed on a node while the node has a local attachment to it. A task of a service on one of
the Swarm's predefined networks, which [network-common.md](network-common.md) defines, is on the
node's own network of that name: its container is attached to that network. No node has a local
attachment to the Swarm's predefined networks. A node creates its load-balancer endpoint on a
network of the `overlay` driver, the ingress network included, with the network, and deletes
it with the network. `GET /networks/{id}` on the node lists that endpoint, with its address,
in `Containers`, as the entry that is not one of the node's containers. Except on an
ingress network, in either form that [The ingress network](#swarm-networking-the-ingress-network) describes, the node
deletes the network once no task or standalone container of the node is on it, so the load-balancer
endpoint does not outlast them. A node keeps its local attachment to an ingress network after its
last task on that network is gone. Unless an expectation or its section names other values, an
expectation holds in a Swarm with the cluster settings that `POST /swarm/init` sets by
default. An expectation holds whatever data-path, advertise and listen addresses each node gives in
`POST /swarm/init` or `POST /swarm/join`, when the data-path addresses of the
Swarm's nodes are all of one IP version, and when each node's route for its VXLAN traffic to the
other nodes selects its data-path address as the source address
([*SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-NOT-DATA-PATH*](#SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-NOT-DATA-PATH)), unless the expectation names that case. An
expectation about traffic between nodes holds for a Linux node and a Windows node only when their
data-path addresses are IPv4 ([*SWARM-EW-WINDOWS-V6-DATA-PATH*](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-EW-WINDOWS-V6-DATA-PATH)).

An expectation that involves the ingress network holds for an ingress network that was created with
`Ingress` set, that is not `internal` and that does not have the option `dsr`.
Only an expectation that names an ingress network without `Ingress` covers such a network
([The ingress network](#swarm-networking-the-ingress-network)). An expectation about a request, or a command that
makes one, that gives a service a published port in ingress mode, whether the request sets that mode
or the daemon stores the port in ingress mode because `PublishMode` is unset or is a
value that the API reference does not list, holds for a request whose service spec is in the `vip`
endpoint mode, in a Swarm where an ingress network exists. Only an expectation that names a spec in
the `dnsrr` endpoint mode or a Swarm without an ingress network covers those cases
([*SWARM-INGPUB-DNSRR-REFUSED*](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-INGPUB-DNSRR-REFUSED), [*SWARM-INGRESS-ABSENT-PUBLISH*](#SWARM-INGRESS-ABSENT-PUBLISH)). An expectation that
involves a node's gateway network holds for one that the daemon created, or that the operator
created with the options of one that the daemon creates and no others but a subnet and a gateway
([Gateway network](swarm-traffic.md#swarm-traffic-gateway-network) in [swarm-traffic.md](swarm-traffic.md)), unless the
expectation names other options. The daemon creates its gateway network with
`com.docker.network.bridge.name` set to `docker_gwbridge`,
`com.docker.network.bridge.enable_icc` set to `false` and
`com.docker.network.bridge.enable_ip_masquerade` set to `true`. On an overlay network with
more than one subnet, an expectation about traffic to a VIP holds for the VIP and a backend task
only when both are in the subnet of the load-balancer endpoint of the client's node on that network
([*SWARM-EW-VIP-MULTIPLE-SUBNETS*](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-EW-VIP-MULTIPLE-SUBNETS)). On Linux nodes, an expectation about a
`mode=host` published port holds for a service that is attached to at least one network
that is not `internal`, and for a service whose spec names no network and that publishes no port
in ingress mode, since its tasks run on the default bridge network
([*SWARM-EGRESS-NO-NETWORK-DEFAULT-BRIDGE*](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-EGRESS-NO-NETWORK-DEFAULT-BRIDGE)). An expectation about reaching a
`mode=host` published port at an address of the node holds on a network whose gateway
mode for that address's family is not `routed`, with
`com.docker.network.bridge.host_binding_ipv4` unset or `0.0.0.0` and without
`com.docker.network.bridge.inhibit_ipv4`, unless the expectation names them
([bridge-networking.md](bridge-networking.md)).

<a id="swarm-networking-requirements"></a>

## Requirements

<a id="REQ-SWARM-ATTACH-FAILURE-START"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-ATTACH-FAILURE-START**: A container whose network attachment fails does not start

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* api/openapi.yaml: operation ContainerStart; https://docs.docker.com/engine/containers/run/#exit-status; https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/23.0/#2303

*Refined by:* [SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CTR-START](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CTR-START), [SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CTR-START-CLI](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CTR-START-CLI), [SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CTR-START-REFUSED](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CTR-START-REFUSED), [SWARM-ENC-NO-XFRM-CTR-START](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-ENC-NO-XFRM-CTR-START), [SWARM-ENC-NO-XFRM-CTR-START-CLI](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-ENC-NO-XFRM-CTR-START-CLI), [SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-IN-USE](#SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-IN-USE), [SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-IN-USE-CLI](#SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-IN-USE-CLI), [SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE](#SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE), [SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-CLI](#SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-CLI), [SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-CTR-START](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-CTR-START), [SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-CTR-START-CLI](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-CTR-START-CLI), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-START](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-START), [SWARM-SCOPED-NOT-ATTACHABLE-START](#SWARM-SCOPED-NOT-ATTACHABLE-START), [SWARM-SCOPED-NOT-ATTACHABLE-START-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-NOT-ATTACHABLE-START-CLI) · *Violated by:* [SWARM-ENC-XFRM-ALGORITHM-UNCHECKED](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-ENC-XFRM-ALGORITHM-UNCHECKED)

When the daemon cannot attach a container to its network, the start request fails with an error
response, and docker run exits non-zero (125 for a daemon error).

<a id="REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOLS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOLS**: An overlay network without a subnet gets one from the default address pools

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/swarm-mode/#configuring-default-address-pools; https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#using-custom-default-address-pools; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/swarm/init/#default-addr-pool; https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/System/operation/SystemInfo

*Refined by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOL-ALLOCATION](#SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOL-ALLOCATION), [SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER](#SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER), [SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER-CLI](#SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER-CLI), [SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER-DEFAULT-POOL](#SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER-DEFAULT-POOL), [SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER-DEFAULT-POOL-CLI](#SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER-DEFAULT-POOL-CLI), [SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID](#SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID), [SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID-CLI](#SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID-CLI) · *Violated by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-WITHOUT-POOL-DROPPED](#SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-WITHOUT-POOL-DROPPED), [SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-ZERO-UNALLOCATED](#SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-ZERO-UNALLOCATED)

An overlay network created without a subnet gets a subnet allocated from the default address
pools set at swarm init, 10.0.0.0/8 by default, with the configured mask length, /24 by default.
The subnet size is at most 29.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-CONTROL-ENCRYPTED"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-CONTROL-ENCRYPTED**: Swarm control and management plane traffic is always encrypted

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#swarm-and-types-of-traffic; https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#encryption

*Refined by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-GOSSIP-NO-CLEARTEXT](#SWARM-CLUSTER-GOSSIP-NO-CLEARTEXT), [SWARM-CLUSTER-MANAGEMENT-NO-CLEARTEXT](#SWARM-CLUSTER-MANAGEMENT-NO-CLEARTEXT)

Management and control plane traffic between Swarm nodes is always encrypted, whether or not
application data on an overlay network is encrypted.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS**: DataPathAddr sets the address peers send a node's overlay traffic to

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/swarm/init/#data-path-addr; https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#use-a-separate-interface-for-control-and-data-traffic; https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/Swarm/operation/SwarmInit; https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/25.0/#2500; https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/Swarm/operation/SwarmJoin; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/swarm/init/#advertise-addr

*Refined by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-ADVERTISE-ADDRESS-IFACE](#SWARM-CLUSTER-ADVERTISE-ADDRESS-IFACE), [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS), [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-DEFAULT](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-DEFAULT), [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-V6](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-V6) · *Violated by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-ADVERTISE-IFACE-RESOLVED-ONCE](#SWARM-CLUSTER-ADVERTISE-IFACE-RESOLVED-ONCE), [SWARM-CLUSTER-IFACE-NAME-RESOLVED-ONCE](#SWARM-CLUSTER-IFACE-NAME-RESOLVED-ONCE), [SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS](#SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS), [SWARM-EW-WINDOWS-V6-DATA-PATH](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-EW-WINDOWS-V6-DATA-PATH)

The data-path address given at swarm init or join, an IPv4 or IPv6 address or an interface, is
the address other nodes use to reach the node's containers, so that data traffic can be
separated from management traffic. Without it, the advertise address is used. When the data-path
address or the advertise address is given as an interface, traffic among a service's containers
is sent over the data-path interface, and traffic about joining, leaving and managing the Swarm
over the advertise interface. Overlay networks are supported over an IPv6 transport.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT**: The data-path port is set at init, 1024 to 49151, default 4789

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/swarm/init/#data-path-port; https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/Swarm/operation/SwarmInit; https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/overlay/#requirements

*Refined by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT), [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-DEFAULT](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-DEFAULT), [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID), [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID-CLI](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID-CLI), [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-ZERO](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-ZERO), [SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER](#SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER), [SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER-CLI](#SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER-CLI) · *Violated by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-PORT](#SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-PORT)

The UDP port for overlay data traffic is set at swarm init and applies to every node of the
swarm. It must be in the range 1024 to 49151; when it is unset or 0, the default port 4789 is
used, and docker info reports the configured port.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-GOSSIP-PORTS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-GOSSIP-PORTS**: Nodes discover each other's networks on TCP and UDP port 7946

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/overlay/#requirements; https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#firewall-considerations; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/swarm/init/#advertise-addr; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/swarm/init/#listen-addr

*Refined by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-GOSSIP-ADVERTISE-ADDRESS](#SWARM-CLUSTER-GOSSIP-ADVERTISE-ADDRESS), [SWARM-CLUSTER-GOSSIP-LISTEN-ADDRESS](#SWARM-CLUSTER-GOSSIP-LISTEN-ADDRESS)

Nodes exchange container network discovery traffic on TCP and UDP port 7946. A node is reached
at the address it advertises to the other members for overlay networking.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-DATA-PATH-VXLAN"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-DATA-PATH-VXLAN**: Overlay traffic between nodes is VXLAN to the data-path port

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/overlay/#requirements; https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#firewall-considerations; https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/swarm-tutorial/#open-protocols-and-ports-between-the-hosts; https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/24.0/#2403

*Refined by:* [SWARM-WIRECLEAR-ETHERNET-PAYLOAD](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-WIRECLEAR-ETHERNET-PAYLOAD), [SWARM-WIRECLEAR-UDP-PORT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-WIRECLEAR-UDP-PORT), [SWARM-WIRECLEAR-VXLAN-VNI](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-WIRECLEAR-VXLAN-VNI), [SWARM-WIREENC-ETHERNET-PAYLOAD](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-WIREENC-ETHERNET-PAYLOAD), [SWARM-WIREENC-UDP-PORT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-WIREENC-UDP-PORT), [SWARM-WIREENC-VXLAN-VNI](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-WIREENC-VXLAN-VNI) · *Violated by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-PORT](#SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-PORT)

Overlay traffic between nodes, the ingress network included, is VXLAN over UDP to the Swarm
data-path port: 4789 by default, configurable at swarm init. Encrypted overlays use the
configured data-path port too.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-CREATED-AT-INIT"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-CREATED-AT-INIT**: Swarm init or join creates the ingress network on each node

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#overlay-networking; https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#key-network-concepts; https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/overlay/#use-the-default-overlay-network

*Refined by:* [SWARM-INGRESS-DEFAULT](#SWARM-INGRESS-DEFAULT), [SWARM-INGRESS-LIST-EVERY-NODE](#SWARM-INGRESS-LIST-EVERY-NODE)

When a swarm is initialized or a node joins one, an overlay network called ingress is created on
that node to carry routing-mesh traffic; every node of the swarm lists it.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-LEGACY-FORM"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-LEGACY-FORM**: An overlay named ingress with the internal label is the ingress network

*Source kind:* issue · *Source:* https://github.com/moby/swarmkit/pull/2028: the maintainers' request that the API definition of the flag say so; swarmkit api/specs.proto: NetworkSpec.Ingress

*Refined by:* [SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-ANY-VALUE](#SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-ANY-VALUE), [SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-DELETE-IN-USE](#SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-DELETE-IN-USE), [SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-IS-INGRESS](#SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-IS-INGRESS), [SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-PUBLISH](#SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-PUBLISH), [SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-SERVICE-NETWORK](#SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-SERVICE-NETWORK)

Ingress networks created before the Ingress flag existed have the name ingress and the label
com.docker.swarm.internal instead of the flag. Such a network is the ingress network.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-MESH-ONLY"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-MESH-ONLY**: The ingress network carries the routing mesh's published-port traffic

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#key-network-concepts; https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/prior-releases/#1122-2016-10-11

*Refined by:* [SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-SERVICE-NETWORK](#SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-SERVICE-NETWORK), [SWARM-INGRESS-SERVICE-NETWORK](#SWARM-INGRESS-SERVICE-NETWORK), [SWARM-INGRESS-SERVICE-NETWORK-CLI](#SWARM-INGRESS-SERVICE-NETWORK-CLI), [SWARM-SD-INGRESS-ONLY](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-SD-INGRESS-ONLY)

The ingress network exists to carry published-port traffic of the routing mesh. Service
discovery is disabled on it and services cannot be placed on it as a regular network.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-NOT-FOR-SERVICES"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-NOT-FOR-SERVICES**: A service cannot name the ingress network as one of its networks

*Source kind:* api · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/Service/operation/ServiceCreate; https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#customize-ingress

*Refined by:* [SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-SERVICE-NETWORK](#SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-SERVICE-NETWORK), [SWARM-INGRESS-SERVICE-NETWORK](#SWARM-INGRESS-SERVICE-NETWORK), [SWARM-INGRESS-SERVICE-NETWORK-CLI](#SWARM-INGRESS-SERVICE-NETWORK-CLI)

Service create and update refuse a network that is not eligible for services; the ingress
network is reached only through published ports.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-OVERLAY-ONLY"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-OVERLAY-ONLY**: The ingress network is an overlay network and cannot be attachable

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/create/#ingress; https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version-history/#v129-api-changes; api/openapi.yaml: operation NetworkCreate

*Refined by:* [SWARM-INGRESS-ATTACHABLE](#SWARM-INGRESS-ATTACHABLE), [SWARM-INGRESS-ATTACHABLE-CLI](#SWARM-INGRESS-ATTACHABLE-CLI), [SWARM-INGRESS-CUSTOM-MTU](#SWARM-INGRESS-CUSTOM-MTU), [SWARM-INGRESS-NODE-LOCAL-DRIVER](#SWARM-INGRESS-NODE-LOCAL-DRIVER), [SWARM-INGRESS-NODE-LOCAL-DRIVER-CLI](#SWARM-INGRESS-NODE-LOCAL-DRIVER-CLI), [SWARM-INGRESS-PLUGIN-DRIVER](#SWARM-INGRESS-PLUGIN-DRIVER), [SWARM-INGRESS-PLUGIN-DRIVER-CLI](#SWARM-INGRESS-PLUGIN-DRIVER-CLI) · *Violated by:* [SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-NODE-LOCAL-DRIVER](#SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-NODE-LOCAL-DRIVER), [SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-PARTLY-SUPPORTED](#SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-PARTLY-SUPPORTED)

Creating the ingress network is supported only with the overlay driver. Any overlay option is
available for it except --attachable.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-DRIVER-NOT-IMPLEMENTED"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-DRIVER-NOT-IMPLEMENTED**: An ingress network with a driver other than overlay is refused with 501

*Source kind:* issue · *Source:* https://github.com/moby/swarmkit/pull/2028: the merged change that lets the ingress network be replaced

*Refined by:* [SWARM-INGRESS-PLUGIN-DRIVER](#SWARM-INGRESS-PLUGIN-DRIVER)

Creating an ingress network with a driver other than overlay is refused as not implemented, with
status 501.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-REMOVE-CONFIRM"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-REMOVE-CONFIRM**: docker network rm asks before it removes the ingress network

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#customize-ingress

*Refined by:* [SWARM-INGRESS-DELETE-DECLINED](#SWARM-INGRESS-DELETE-DECLINED)

docker network rm for the ingress network prints a warning and asks the user to confirm, with no
as the default answer ([y/N]).

<a id="REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-REPLACEABLE"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-REPLACEABLE**: The ingress network can be removed and recreated with custom options

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#customize-ingress; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/create/#ingress; https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/31714

*Refined by:* [SWARM-INGRESS-ABSENT-PUBLISH](#SWARM-INGRESS-ABSENT-PUBLISH), [SWARM-INGRESS-CUSTOM-MTU](#SWARM-INGRESS-CUSTOM-MTU), [SWARM-INGRESS-CUSTOM-SUBNET](#SWARM-INGRESS-CUSTOM-SUBNET), [SWARM-INGRESS-CUSTOM-SUBNET-REACHABLE](#SWARM-INGRESS-CUSTOM-SUBNET-REACHABLE), [SWARM-INGRESS-DELETE-IN-USE](#SWARM-INGRESS-DELETE-IN-USE), [SWARM-INGRESS-DELETE-IN-USE-CLI](#SWARM-INGRESS-DELETE-IN-USE-CLI), [SWARM-INGRESS-DELETE-UNUSED](#SWARM-INGRESS-DELETE-UNUSED), [SWARM-INGRESS-DELETE-UNUSED-CLI](#SWARM-INGRESS-DELETE-UNUSED-CLI), [SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-DELETE-IN-USE](#SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-DELETE-IN-USE), [SWARM-INGRESS-LIST-EVERY-NODE](#SWARM-INGRESS-LIST-EVERY-NODE), [SWARM-INGRESS-REPLACEMENT](#SWARM-INGRESS-REPLACEMENT), [SWARM-INGRESS-REPLACEMENT-CLI](#SWARM-INGRESS-REPLACEMENT-CLI)

Once no service publishes ports through it, the ingress network can be removed and recreated
with --ingress, under any name and with a custom subnet, gateway and options. While no ingress
network exists, services cannot publish ports through the routing mesh.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-SINGLE"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-SINGLE**: A swarm has at most one ingress network

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#customize-ingress; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/create/#ingress

*Refined by:* [SWARM-INGRESS-DUPLICATE](#SWARM-INGRESS-DUPLICATE), [SWARM-INGRESS-DUPLICATE-CLI](#SWARM-INGRESS-DUPLICATE-CLI), [SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-IS-INGRESS](#SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-IS-INGRESS) · *Violated by:* [SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-PARTLY-SUPPORTED](#SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-PARTLY-SUPPORTED), [SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-SECOND](#SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-SECOND)

Only one ingress network can exist at a time; an attempt to create a second one fails.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-MIXED-VERSION-INTEROP"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-MIXED-VERSION-INTEROP**: Nodes of different engine releases share overlay and ingress networks

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/29/#2921; https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/18.02/#18020-ce; https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#customize-ingress

*Refined by:* [SWARM-RESTART-OTHER-NODES](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-RESTART-OTHER-NODES), [SWARM-WIRE-MIXED-VERSIONS](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-WIRE-MIXED-VERSIONS)

A Swarm is upgraded node by node, so nodes of different releases share overlay and ingress
networks during the rollout. During the rollout, traffic between nodes of different releases
passes on the ingress network and on overlay networks. On an encrypted overlay network it passes
too, except between a node of 29.2.1 or later and a node of 29.0.0 to 29.2.0, 28.2.2, 25.0.14 or
25.0.13.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-ATTACHABLE"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-ATTACHABLE**: Standalone containers attach only to attachable Swarm networks

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/create/; https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/overlay/#attach-a-container-to-an-overlay-network; https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/Network/operation/NetworkConnect

*Refined by:* [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT), [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-CLI), [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START), [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-CLI), [SWARM-SCOPED-NOT-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT](#SWARM-SCOPED-NOT-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT), [SWARM-SCOPED-NOT-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-NOT-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-CLI), [SWARM-SCOPED-NOT-ATTACHABLE-START](#SWARM-SCOPED-NOT-ATTACHABLE-START), [SWARM-SCOPED-NOT-ATTACHABLE-START-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-NOT-ATTACHABLE-START-CLI) · *Violated by:* [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-RETRY-SKIPS-ATTACHMENT](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-RETRY-SKIPS-ATTACHMENT), [SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-STANDALONE-ATTACH](#SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-STANDALONE-ATTACH)

By default a Swarm-scoped network accepts only Swarm services. Created with Attachable, it also
accepts standalone containers through docker run and docker network connect, on any node of the
swarm.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-ATTACHMENT-RELEASED"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-ATTACHMENT-RELEASED**: A container leaving a Swarm network releases its attachment

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/overlay/#use-an-overlay-network-for-standalone-containers; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/rm/

*Refined by:* [SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-RELEASED](#SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-RELEASED), [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-LAST-DETACH-DELETE](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-LAST-DETACH-DELETE), [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHMENT-TASK-REMOVED](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHMENT-TASK-REMOVED)

When a standalone container on an attachable Swarm network stops or is disconnected, the network
is released on that node, and once no container uses the network it can be removed.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-CONFIG-FROM"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-CONFIG-FROM**: A Swarm network of a local driver takes each node's config-only network

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/create/#swarm-networks-with-local-scope-drivers; https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/Network/operation/NetworkCreate

*Refined by:* [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-INSPECT-ATTACHED](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-INSPECT-ATTACHED), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-CONNECT](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-CONNECT), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-START](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-START), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-TASKS](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-TASKS), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-SUBNET](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-SUBNET), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-TASKS](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-TASKS), [SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE](#SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE)

A network of a node-local driver can be promoted to scope swarm and used by services.
Node-specific configuration, such as the subnet, comes from a config-only network of the name
that --config-from gives, which is created on each node.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-CREATE-ON-MANAGER"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-CREATE-ON-MANAGER**: Swarm-scoped networks are created on a manager

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/services/#connect-the-service-to-an-overlay-network; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/create/; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/create/#swarm-networks-with-local-scope-drivers; https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/Network/operation/NetworkCreate

*Refined by:* [SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CREATE-RECREATE](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CREATE-RECREATE), [SWARM-OVL-UNALLOCATED-LISTED](#SWARM-OVL-UNALLOCATED-LISTED), [SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE](#SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE), [SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-ALLOCATED](#SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-ALLOCATED), [SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-CLI), [SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-WORKER](#SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-WORKER), [SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-WORKER-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-WORKER-CLI)

Once swarm mode is enabled, an overlay network, or a network of another driver with scope swarm,
is created on a manager node with docker network create; the network then exists for the whole
swarm.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-DELETE"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-DELETE**: A network with no containers can be removed, also with only dead tasks

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/rm/; https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/17.03/#17031-ce

*Refined by:* [SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CREATE](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CREATE), [SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CTR-START](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CTR-START), [SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CTR-START-CLI](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CTR-START-CLI), [SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CTR-START-REFUSED](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CTR-START-REFUSED), [SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-SHUTDOWN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-SHUTDOWN), [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-LAST-DETACH-DELETE](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-LAST-DETACH-DELETE), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-ONLY-DELETE-UNUSED](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-ONLY-DELETE-UNUSED), [SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-DEAD-TASKS](#SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-DEAD-TASKS)

A network can be removed once no container is connected to it, also when only dead tasks
reference it.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-DELETE-IN-USE"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-DELETE-IN-USE**: A Swarm network that a service uses is not removed

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#customize-ingress; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/create/#ingress; api/openapi.yaml: operation NetworkDelete

*Refined by:* [SWARM-INGRESS-DELETE-IN-USE](#SWARM-INGRESS-DELETE-IN-USE), [SWARM-INGRESS-DELETE-IN-USE-CLI](#SWARM-INGRESS-DELETE-IN-USE-CLI), [SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-DELETE-IN-USE](#SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-DELETE-IN-USE), [SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-SERVICE](#SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-SERVICE), [SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-SERVICE-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-SERVICE-CLI), [SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-TASK](#SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-TASK), [SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-TASK-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-TASK-CLI) · *Violated by:* [SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-DELETE-NOT-FOUND](#SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-DELETE-NOT-FOUND)

A Swarm network can be removed only once the services that use it are removed. DELETE
/networks/{id} for a Swarm-scoped network that a service or a task uses responds 400.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-DRIVER-OPTIONS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-DRIVER-OPTIONS**: Overlay options select encryption, direct server return and the MTU

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#encryption; https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#use-direct-server-return; https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#customize-ingress; https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/overlay/#encrypt-traffic-on-an-overlay-network

*Refined by:* [SWARM-INGRESS-CUSTOM-MTU](#SWARM-INGRESS-CUSTOM-MTU), [SWARM-OVLOPT-DSR](#SWARM-OVLOPT-DSR), [SWARM-OVLOPT-ENCRYPTED](#SWARM-OVLOPT-ENCRYPTED), [SWARM-OVLOPT-FLAG-ANY-VALUE](#SWARM-OVLOPT-FLAG-ANY-VALUE), [SWARM-OVLOPT-MTU](#SWARM-OVLOPT-MTU) · *Violated by:* [SWARM-CTR-WINDOWS-ENCRYPTION](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-CTR-WINDOWS-ENCRYPTION), [SWARM-CTR-WINDOWS-MTU-OPTION](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-CTR-WINDOWS-MTU-OPTION), [SWARM-LB-WINDOWS-DSR](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-LB-WINDOWS-DSR)

When an overlay network is created, the encrypted option enables IPsec encryption of its
application data, the dsr option makes east-west load balancing use direct server return, and
com.docker.network.driver.mtu sets its MTU.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-IPAM-STATUS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-IPAM-STATUS**: Network inspect reports per-subnet IPAM usage from API 1.52 only

*Source kind:* api · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version-history/#v152-api-changes; https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/Network/operation/NetworkInspect

*Refined by:* [SWARM-OVL-STATUS-API-VERSION](#SWARM-OVL-STATUS-API-VERSION), [SWARM-OVL-STATUS-IN-USE](#SWARM-OVL-STATUS-IN-USE), [SWARM-OVL-STATUS-PER-SUBNET](#SWARM-OVL-STATUS-PER-SUBNET), [SWARM-OVL-STATUS-TOTAL](#SWARM-OVL-STATUS-TOTAL) · *Violated by:* [SWARM-OVL-STATUS-FULL-ID](#SWARM-OVL-STATUS-FULL-ID), [SWARM-OVL-STATUS-WORKER](#SWARM-OVL-STATUS-WORKER)

From API 1.52, GET /networks/{id} includes a Status field with, for each subnet of the network,
the number of addresses in use or reserved and the number available for dynamic allocation. At
earlier API versions, the response does not include Status.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-PLUGIN-DRIVERS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-PLUGIN-DRIVERS**: Managed network plugins work in Swarm mode, legacy plugins do not

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/extend/plugins_network/#network-plugins-and-swarm-mode; moby/moby docs/extend/plugins_services.md: section Network plugins

*Refined by:* [SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE](#SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE), [SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-CREATE-MISSING](#SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-CREATE-MISSING), [SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-LEGACY](#SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-LEGACY), [SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-PLACEMENT](#SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-PLACEMENT) · *Violated by:* [SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-LEADER-MISSING](#SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-LEADER-MISSING), [SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-ON-LEADER](#SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-ON-LEADER), [SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-UNTAGGED-IPAM](#SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-UNTAGGED-IPAM), [SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-UNTAGGED-NAME](#SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-UNTAGGED-NAME)

Network plugins of the v2 plugin system work in swarm mode when installed on the nodes, and
plugin availability determines where networks are created and tasks are scheduled. Legacy
plugins do not work in swarm mode.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-SCOPE-VISIBLE"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-SCOPE-VISIBLE**: Every manager lists a Swarm network with scope swarm

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/services/#connect-the-service-to-an-overlay-network; https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#create-an-overlay-network; https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/Network/operation/NetworkInspect; https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version-history/#v129-api-changes

*Refined by:* [SWARM-SCOPED-INSPECT](#SWARM-SCOPED-INSPECT), [SWARM-SCOPED-INSPECT-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-INSPECT-CLI), [SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-MANAGER](#SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-MANAGER), [SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-MANAGER-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-MANAGER-CLI), [SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-SCOPE-FILTER](#SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-SCOPE-FILTER), [SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-LIST](#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-LIST), [SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-SCOPE-FILTER](#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-SCOPE-FILTER)

After an overlay network is created in swarm mode, all manager nodes have access to it, and
network ls and network inspect report its driver and the scope swarm. The scope parameter of the
network list and inspect requests selects networks by scope.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-SERVICE-VIP"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-SERVICE-VIP**: A vip-mode service has a VIP on each overlay network it is attached to

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#configure-service-discovery; https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/Service/operation/ServiceInspect

*Refined by:* [SWARM-OVL-VIP-INGRESS](#SWARM-OVL-VIP-INGRESS), [SWARM-OVL-VIP-LEADER-CHANGE](#SWARM-OVL-VIP-LEADER-CHANGE), [SWARM-OVL-VIP-PER-NETWORK](#SWARM-OVL-VIP-PER-NETWORK), [SWARM-OVL-VIP-PER-NETWORK-CLI](#SWARM-OVL-VIP-PER-NETWORK-CLI), [SWARM-OVL-VIP-UPDATE](#SWARM-OVL-VIP-UPDATE)

A service in the default vip endpoint mode is assigned a virtual IP, the front end that clients
use to reach it, on each overlay network it is attached to; the service's Endpoint reports these
VirtualIPs with their network IDs.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-SERVICE-VIP-KEPT"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-SERVICE-VIP-KEPT**: A vip-mode service keeps its VIP on a network while it stays attached

*Source kind:* observable · *Source:* Clients that resolve a service's name once and keep connecting to that address (such as a reverse proxy that resolves its upstream at startup) and clients that cache the embedded DNS server's answer for its TTL of 600 seconds. They keep using a service's VIP across updates of the service and changes of leader

*Refined by:* [SWARM-OVL-VIP-LEADER-CHANGE](#SWARM-OVL-VIP-LEADER-CHANGE), [SWARM-OVL-VIP-UPDATE](#SWARM-OVL-VIP-UPDATE)

A service in vip endpoint mode keeps its VIP on a network while it stays in vip mode and
attached to that network.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-STATIC-ADDRESS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-STATIC-ADDRESS**: A static address that is not available makes the container fail to start

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/connect/#ip; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/connect/#network-implications-of-stopping-pausing-or-restarting-containers

*Refined by:* [SWARM-OVL-IPRANGE](#SWARM-OVL-IPRANGE), [SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-IN-USE](#SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-IN-USE), [SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-IN-USE-CLI](#SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-IN-USE-CLI), [SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE](#SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE), [SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-CLI](#SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-CLI), [SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-RELEASED](#SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-RELEASED)

A container's requested IP address on a network is applied when it starts; if the address is no
longer available, the container fails to start. An address from outside the network's IP range
is not given to another container while its holder is off the network.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-SUBNET-CONFIG"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-SUBNET-CONFIG**: An overlay network uses the subnet, gateway and IP range it is given

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#configure-the-subnet-and-gateway; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/create/

*Refined by:* [SWARM-INGRESS-CUSTOM-SUBNET](#SWARM-INGRESS-CUSTOM-SUBNET), [SWARM-OVL-IPRANGE](#SWARM-OVL-IPRANGE) · *Violated by:* [SWARM-OVL-ALLOCATION-FAILURE-UNREPORTED](#SWARM-OVL-ALLOCATION-FAILURE-UNREPORTED), [SWARM-OVL-V6-ADDRESSING](#SWARM-OVL-V6-ADDRESSING)

An overlay network can be created with its own subnets, gateways and IP ranges in place of an
allocated subnet. Container addresses, and the other IP addresses that the network allocates,
then come from the IP range.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-UNALLOCATED-ISOLATED"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-UNALLOCATED-ISOLATED**: A network that is not allocated does not break requests about others

*Source kind:* issue · *Source:* https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53325

*Refined by:* [SWARM-OVL-UNALLOCATED-OTHERS-LISTED](#SWARM-OVL-UNALLOCATED-OTHERS-LISTED)

A Swarm network whose allocation is pending or failed must not make network list or inspect
requests fail for other, healthy networks.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-VERBOSE-INSPECT"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-VERBOSE-INSPECT**: Verbose network inspect shows each service's VIP, ports and tasks

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/inspect/#options; https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version-history/#v128-api-changes; https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/Network/operation/NetworkInspect

*Refined by:* [SWARM-OVL-VERBOSE-SERVICES](#SWARM-OVL-VERBOSE-SERVICES), [SWARM-OVL-VERBOSE-SERVICES-CLI](#SWARM-OVL-VERBOSE-SERVICES-CLI), [SWARM-OVL-VERBOSE-TASKS](#SWARM-OVL-VERBOSE-TASKS), [SWARM-OVL-VERBOSE-VIP](#SWARM-OVL-VERBOSE-VIP)

For swarm overlay networks, verbose network inspect shows service details: each service's VIP
and port mappings and the addresses of its tasks, local and non-local.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-WORKER-ON-DEMAND"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-WORKER-ON-DEMAND**: A Swarm network is extended to a worker that uses it

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/services/#connect-the-service-to-an-overlay-network; https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/overlay/#use-an-overlay-network-for-standalone-containers

*Refined by:* [SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-WORKER](#SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-WORKER) · *Violated by:* [SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-LOCAL](#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-LOCAL)

A Swarm network is extended to a worker when a service task or an attached container on that
worker needs it.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-CONNECTIVITY"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-CONNECTIVITY**: Containers on a shared overlay reach each other across nodes

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#attach-a-service-to-an-overlay-network; https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/overlay/; https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/overlay/#container-discovery; https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/18.03/#18030-ce

*Refined by:* [SWARM-ENC-CLEARTEXT-PASSES](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-ENC-CLEARTEXT-PASSES), [SWARM-ENC-KEY-ROTATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-ENC-KEY-ROTATION), [SWARM-ENC-VNI-REUSE](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-ENC-VNI-REUSE), [SWARM-ENC-VNI-REUSE-KILLED-DAEMON](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-ENC-VNI-REUSE-KILLED-DAEMON), [SWARM-ENC-VNI-REUSE-WINDOWS](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-ENC-VNI-REUSE-WINDOWS), [SWARM-EW-CROSS-SUBNET](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-EW-CROSS-SUBNET), [SWARM-EW-PROTOCOLS](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-EW-PROTOCOLS), [SWARM-EW-UNICAST](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-EW-UNICAST), [SWARM-LB-TASK-ADDRESS](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-LB-TASK-ADDRESS), [SWARM-RESTART-KILLED-VNI-REUSE](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-RESTART-KILLED-VNI-REUSE), [SWARM-SCALE-MANY-NETWORKS](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-MANY-NETWORKS), [SWARM-WIRE-ADDRESS-ASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-WIRE-ADDRESS-ASSIGNMENT) · *Violated by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-MIXED-VERSIONS-ACCEPTED](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-MIXED-VERSIONS-ACCEPTED), [SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-NOT-DATA-PATH](#SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-NOT-DATA-PATH), [SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-PORT](#SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-PORT), [SWARM-CTR-WINDOWS-ENCRYPTION](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-CTR-WINDOWS-ENCRYPTION), [SWARM-ENC-XFRM-ALGORITHM-UNCHECKED](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-ENC-XFRM-ALGORITHM-UNCHECKED), [SWARM-EW-ESP-SEQUENCE-EXHAUSTION](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-EW-ESP-SEQUENCE-EXHAUSTION), [SWARM-EW-WINDOWS-V6-DATA-PATH](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-EW-WINDOWS-V6-DATA-PATH), [SWARM-SCALE-WINDOWS-SCTP](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-WINDOWS-SCTP)

Services and containers attached to the same overlay network communicate with each other across
it, whichever nodes they run on; Docker routes each packet to the destination container
transparently. Port mappings on overlays cover TCP, UDP and SCTP.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-PEERS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-PEERS**: Overlay inspect lists the network's peer nodes at their advertise addresses

*Source kind:* api · *Source:* api/openapi.yaml: definition Network (Peers); api/openapi.yaml: definition PeerInfo; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/swarm/join/#advertise-addr

*Refined by:* [SWARM-OVL-PEERS](#SWARM-OVL-PEERS)

On a node with a local attachment to an overlay network, GET /networks/{id} lists in Peers the
nodes that have a local attachment to the network. The IP of each entry is the address that the
node advertises to the other members of the Swarm.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-VNI-REPORTED"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-VNI-REPORTED**: Overlay inspect reports the VNIs that the network uses

*Source kind:* observable · *Source:* Operators who read the VNIs of an overlay network in network inspect to match VXLAN traffic to networks in firewall rules and packet captures and to create a network again with the same VNIs. Network inspect is the only place that shows a VNI that the managers allocated; https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/networking/#create-an-overlay-network: example output that shows the option; api/openapi.yaml: definition Network (Options)

*Refined by:* [SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-LONG](#SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-LONG), [SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-REPORTED](#SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-REPORTED), [SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-SHORT](#SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-SHORT), [SWARM-OVLOPT-VNI-LIST](#SWARM-OVLOPT-VNI-LIST)

GET /networks/{id} on a manager reports the VNIs of an overlay network in its vxlanid_list
option.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-VNI-LIST"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-VNI-LIST**: An overlay network's vxlanid_list option sets its VNIs

*Source kind:* observable · *Source:* Operators who pass com.docker.network.driver.overlay.vxlanid_list to docker network create or in a stack file's driver_opts to choose the VNIs that an overlay network's VXLAN traffic carries on the underlay. Network inspect shows the option on every overlay network

*Refined by:* [SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST](#SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST), [SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-LONG](#SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-LONG), [SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-SHORT](#SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-SHORT), [SWARM-OVLOPT-VNI-LIST](#SWARM-OVLOPT-VNI-LIST), [SWARM-SCALE-VNI-REUSE](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-VNI-REUSE)

An overlay network created with the driver option com.docker.network.driver.overlay.vxlanid_list
uses the VNIs in that list, one per subnet in order, and reports them in its options. Subnets
beyond the list get automatic VNIs. A VNI that a deleted network used can be requested again.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-ROUTING-MESH"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-ROUTING-MESH**: An ingress-mode port is reachable on every node, task or not

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/ingress/; https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/services/#publish-a-services-ports-using-the-routing-mesh; api/openapi.yaml: definition EndpointPortConfig (PublishMode); https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/29/#2900

*Refined by:* [NET-API-PRUNE-SWARM-MESH-EGRESS](network-common.md#NET-API-PRUNE-SWARM-MESH-EGRESS), [SWARM-FAILREP-INGRESS-PORT-RECOVERY](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-FAILREP-INGRESS-PORT-RECOVERY), [SWARM-INGPUB-EVERY-NODE](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-INGPUB-EVERY-NODE), [SWARM-INGPUB-FIREWALLD-RELOAD](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-INGPUB-FIREWALLD-RELOAD), [SWARM-INGPUB-FLOW-SAME-TASK](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-INGPUB-FLOW-SAME-TASK), [SWARM-INGRESS-CUSTOM-SUBNET-REACHABLE](#SWARM-INGRESS-CUSTOM-SUBNET-REACHABLE), [SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-PUBLISH](#SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-PUBLISH), [SWARM-RESTART-INGRESS-FROM-OTHER-NODES](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-RESTART-INGRESS-FROM-OTHER-NODES), [SWARM-SCALE-PORT-PROTOCOLS](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-PORT-PROTOCOLS), [SWARM-SCALE-PORT-PROTOCOLS-REMOVAL](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-PORT-PROTOCOLS-REMOVAL) · *Violated by:* [SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-PARTLY-SUPPORTED](#SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-PARTLY-SUPPORTED), [SWARM-LB-ROOTLESS](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-LB-ROOTLESS), [SWARM-PUB-AUTO-ASSIGNED-PORT-HOST-MODE](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-PUB-AUTO-ASSIGNED-PORT-HOST-MODE), [SWARM-PUB-INGRESS-PORT-IN-USE](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-PUB-INGRESS-PORT-IN-USE), [SWARM-SCALE-WINDOWS-SCTP](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-WINDOWS-SCTP)

In ingress mode, every node accepts connections on the published port, whether or not it runs a
task, and routes each connection to an active task. Services stay reachable on published ports
after a firewalld reload.

<a id="REQ-SWARM-TASK-ERRORS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-SWARM-TASK-ERRORS**: A task that cannot run fails or is rejected, and reports its error

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/how-swarm-mode-works/swarm-task-states/; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/service/ps/; api/openapi.yaml: definition TaskStatus (Err)

*Refined by:* [SWARM-ENC-NO-KEYS](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-ENC-NO-KEYS), [SWARM-ENC-NO-XFRM](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-ENC-NO-XFRM), [SWARM-FAILREP-SERVICE-PS](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-FAILREP-SERVICE-PS), [SWARM-INGPUB-INGRESS-RULES-FAILED](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-INGPUB-INGRESS-RULES-FAILED), [SWARM-OVL-NO-VETH](#SWARM-OVL-NO-VETH), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-TASKS](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-TASKS), [SWARM-SCOPED-IFNAME-REFUSED](#SWARM-SCOPED-IFNAME-REFUSED), [SWARM-WIRE-NO-VXLAN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-WIRE-NO-VXLAN) · *Violated by:* [SWARM-OVL-ALLOCATION-FAILURE-UNREPORTED](#SWARM-OVL-ALLOCATION-FAILURE-UNREPORTED), [SWARM-OVL-VNI-DUPLICATE](#SWARM-OVL-VNI-DUPLICATE), [SWARM-OVL-VNI-DUPLICATE-CLI](#SWARM-OVL-VNI-DUPLICATE-CLI), [SWARM-PORTALLOC-PORT-ABOVE-65535](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-PORTALLOC-PORT-ABOVE-65535), [SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-SERVICE](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-SERVICE), [SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-ON-LEADER](#SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-ON-LEADER)

A task advances through states and ends as failed or rejected when it cannot run; a worker can
reject a task, which is then in the REJECTED state. The error appears in the task's status, and
docker service ps lists a service's tasks with their states, and with --no-trunc their full
error messages.

<a id="swarm-networking-rationales"></a>

## Rationales

<a id="RAT-SWARM-AUTO-VNI-ABOVE-VLAN-IDS"></a>

**Rationale RAT-SWARM-AUTO-VNI-ABOVE-VLAN-IDS**: Windows nodes cannot use a VNI in the range of 802.1Q VLAN IDs

*Rationale of:* [SWARM-OVL-VNI-AUTO-RANGE](#SWARM-OVL-VNI-AUTO-RANGE)

Windows does not support VNIs in the range of 802.1Q VLAN IDs, 0 to 4095. The managers choose a
network's VNIs before they know which nodes will attach to it, so they take automatic VNIs from
4096 up. An automatic VNI below 4096 would give an overlay network that Windows nodes cannot
use. A change to the range from which the managers take automatic VNIs should therefore be
deliberate.

<a id="RAT-SWARM-CONFIG-ONLY-PER-NODE"></a>

**Rationale RAT-SWARM-CONFIG-ONLY-PER-NODE**: The managers do not track which nodes have a config-only network

*Rationale of:* [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-ONLY-ONE-NODE](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-ONLY-ONE-NODE)

A config-only network is node-local: each node has its own, and the managers' store does not
record which nodes have one of a given name. The manager that handles a create checks only its
own config-only networks, and the scheduler places a service's tasks without regard to them; the
operator creates them on each node ([*REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-CONFIG-FROM*](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-CONFIG-FROM)). Tracking them would
make the managers depend on node-local state and would change where the tasks of every such
service can run. That change should be made by design, with the placement and the check at
create in view.

<a id="RAT-SWARM-LIVE-RESTORE-REFUSED"></a>

**Rationale RAT-SWARM-LIVE-RESTORE-REFUSED**: Live-restore on a node in a Swarm changes what a daemon restart does to its tasks

*Rationale of:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-LIVE-RESTORE-NO-START](#SWARM-CLUSTER-LIVE-RESTORE-NO-START), [SWARM-CLUSTER-LIVE-RESTORE-REFUSED](#SWARM-CLUSTER-LIVE-RESTORE-REFUSED), [SWARM-CLUSTER-LIVE-RESTORE-REFUSED-CLI](#SWARM-CLUSTER-LIVE-RESTORE-REFUSED-CLI), [SWARM-CLUSTER-LIVE-RESTORE-RELOAD](#SWARM-CLUSTER-LIVE-RESTORE-RELOAD)

The daemon refuses to combine `live-restore` with Swarm mode when a node
initializes or joins a Swarm, and when a daemon in a Swarm starts. A reload of the configuration
that turns `live-restore` on for a node in a Swarm is accepted, and the daemon then
does not start with it. [*SWARM-CLUSTER-LIVE-RESTORE-REFUSED*](#SWARM-CLUSTER-LIVE-RESTORE-REFUSED) and
[*SWARM-CLUSTER-LIVE-RESTORE-NO-START*](#SWARM-CLUSTER-LIVE-RESTORE-NO-START) notice a change that accepts the combination, and
[*SWARM-CLUSTER-LIVE-RESTORE-RELOAD*](#SWARM-CLUSTER-LIVE-RESTORE-RELOAD) notices a change to what the reload does, which is
part of the same decision. The refusal came with the change that made the daemon restore
container networking at start. Older documentation said that the two are not compatible; the
current page says only that live restore does not pertain to Swarm services. Accepting the
combination would change what a daemon restart does to the task containers on the node: they
would keep running across the restart instead of stopping with the daemon, so such a change
should be deliberate.

<a id="RAT-SWARM-NODE-LOCAL-NO-CLUSTER-RECORDS"></a>

**Rationale RAT-SWARM-NODE-LOCAL-NO-CLUSTER-RECORDS**: A node knows of other nodes' tasks only on networks that share records between nodes

*Rationale of:* [SWARM-OVL-VIP-NODE-LOCAL](#SWARM-OVL-VIP-NODE-LOCAL), [SWARM-SD-NODE-LOCAL-NO-SERVICE](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-SD-NODE-LOCAL-NO-SERVICE)

Service names, `tasks.<service>` and service aliases resolve from records that the
nodes of an overlay network share with each other. A Swarm-scoped network of a node-local driver
shares no records between nodes: each node knows only the containers that it runs itself
([*SWARM-SD-NODE-LOCAL*](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-SD-NODE-LOCAL)). A service name that started to resolve there would need a
definition of what it resolves to, and it would hide the same name on the upstream servers,
which answer for it today. Which names exist on a network should change by design. For the same
reason, a service in vip mode on such a network gets no VIP: an entry in its
`Endpoint.VirtualIPs` names the network without an address
([*SWARM-OVL-VIP-NODE-LOCAL*](#SWARM-OVL-VIP-NODE-LOCAL)). A VIP there would need an address that every node's copy of
the network has, while each node takes its subnet from its own config-only network or address
pools, so giving it one should be a decision about what that address means on each node.

<a id="RAT-SWARM-NODE-REPORTS-OWN-STATE"></a>

**Rationale RAT-SWARM-NODE-REPORTS-OWN-STATE**: Some fields of a Swarm-scoped network describe the node that answers, not the cluster

*Rationale of:* [SWARM-OVL-VERBOSE-UNATTACHED](#SWARM-OVL-VERBOSE-UNATTACHED), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-INSPECT-UNATTACHED](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-INSPECT-UNATTACHED), [SWARM-SCOPED-INSPECT-MANAGER-UNATTACHED](#SWARM-SCOPED-INSPECT-MANAGER-UNATTACHED)

A node fills some fields of a Swarm-scoped network from its own state and not from the managers'
store: `Containers`, `Peers` and the services of a verbose inspect from
its own attachment to the network, and, while it has a local attachment to a network created
with `ConfigFrom`, the `IPAM` of that network from its own config-only
network. A node without that state reports the field empty or leaves it out. The same request
therefore gets different answers on different nodes, and each answer describes the node that
gave it. Filling one of these fields from cluster-wide data changes what the field means on
every node. Such a change should be made on purpose, and with the other fields in view.

<a id="RAT-SWARM-PREDEFINED-NETWORKS"></a>

**Rationale RAT-SWARM-PREDEFINED-NETWORKS**: The Swarm's bridge and host networks stand for each node's own network

*Rationale of:* [NET-API-INSPECT-NAME-SWARM-PREDEFINED](network-common.md#NET-API-INSPECT-NAME-SWARM-PREDEFINED), [SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-INSPECT](#SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-INSPECT), [SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-NOT-LISTED](#SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-NOT-LISTED)

A service that names `bridge` or `host` stores the ID of one of the Swarm's
predefined networks, and `GET /services/{id}` and `GET /tasks` report that ID.
The task's container uses the node's own network of that name. The network list leaves the
Swarm's predefined networks out, so that it shows each of `bridge` and `host`
once, as the network that containers use. A lookup by ID finds them, so that the IDs in services
and tasks resolve to a network. A lookup by the name `bridge` or `host`
without `scope` `swarm` finds the node's own network, which is what the name means
on every node. Listing them would show two networks of each name on every manager to the tooling
that reads the list. A lookup by name that matched them would make the names `bridge`
and `host` ambiguous on every manager, and a lookup by ID that did not find them would
leave those IDs without a network. Each of these changes should be made on purpose.

<a id="RAT-SWARM-WORKER-HOLDS-WHAT-IT-USES"></a>

**Rationale RAT-SWARM-WORKER-HOLDS-WHAT-IT-USES**: A worker is given only the cluster state that its own workloads use

*Rationale of:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-WORKER](#SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-WORKER), [SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-WORKER-CLI](#SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-WORKER-CLI), [SWARM-SCOPED-INSPECT-WORKER-UNATTACHED](#SWARM-SCOPED-INSPECT-WORKER-UNATTACHED), [SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-WORKER-UNATTACHED](#SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-WORKER-UNATTACHED)

The managers hold the cluster object and every Swarm-scoped network. A worker has no access to
their store. It is sent a network when a task or an attached container on it uses that network
([*REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-WORKER-ON-DEMAND*](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-WORKER-ON-DEMAND)), and it is not sent the cluster object. What a
worker's API reports follows from what the worker holds. A worker that starts to report
`Swarm.Cluster`, or a network that nothing on it uses, has been given more of the
cluster's state than before. How much of that state reaches the workers is a design decision
about the cluster, and should not change as a side effect.

<a id="swarm-networking-host-requirements"></a>

## Host requirements

The conventions for this section are in [README.md](README.md#readme-host-requirements). The kernel
facilities and programs are requirements of each Linux node. The Windows facilities are requirements
of each Windows node.

*Needed when:* The iptables backend with iptables-legacy, and an `encrypted` overlay
network on a node with an IPv6 data-path address

options:* `IP6_NF_IPTABLES`, `IP6_NF_FILTER`, `IP6_NF_MANGLE`.

network on a node with an IPv6 data-path address

options:* `NF_TABLES`, `NF_TABLES_IPV6`, `NFT_COMPAT`. Before Linux
5.2, `NFT_CHAIN_ROUTE_IPV6` for the `OUTPUT` chain of the mangle table.

<a id="swarm-networking-interop-premise"></a>

## Interop premise

Users upgrade a Swarm node by node, so nodes of different releases share overlay and ingress
networks during a rollout ([*REQ-SWARM-MIXED-VERSION-INTEROP*](#REQ-SWARM-MIXED-VERSION-INTEROP)).

<a id="swarm-networking-cluster-node-configuration"></a>

## Cluster & node configuration

These expectations cover cluster configuration. The accepted range of the data-path port is 1024 to
49151. A data-path port of 0 is also accepted, and selects the default port 4789. In these
expectations, a data-path port outside the accepted range is a port other than 0 that is less than
1024 or greater than 49151. The reference for `docker swarm init --data-path-port` documents
this range and the default. `AdvertiseAddr`, `DataPathAddr` and
`ListenAddr` in `POST /swarm/init` or `POST /swarm/join` can name a
network interface in place of an IP address. An expectation about such a field holds for an
interface that has at most one IPv4 address and at most one IPv6 address, link-local addresses
included. The address of such an interface is its IPv4 address when it has one, and its IPv6 address
otherwise. The host part of a listen address that names an interface is that address. With the
default `ListenAddr`, `0.0.0.0:2377`, the host part is `0.0.0.0`, and a node that
listens on it listens on every IPv4 and IPv6 address of the node.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS**: DataPathAddr sets the address peers send the node's VXLAN traffic to

*Observed from:* underlay (outer destination address) · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT), [SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN) · *Does not cover:* A DataPathAddr interface is resolved to an address once, at init or join ([SWARM-CLUSTER-IFACE-NAME-RESOLVED-ONCE](#SWARM-CLUSTER-IFACE-NAME-RESOLVED-ONCE)) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-NOT-DATA-PATH](#SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-NOT-DATA-PATH), [SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS](#SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS)

`DataPathAddr` in `POST /swarm/init` or `POST /swarm/join` sets the
address peers send the node's VXLAN traffic to.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-DEFAULT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-DEFAULT**: Without DataPathAddr, peers send VXLAN traffic to the advertise address

*Observed from:* underlay (outer destination address) · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT), [SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN) · *Does not cover:* A Windows node's tunnel endpoint is its HNS management address, not DataPathAddr ([SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS](#SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS))

Without `DataPathAddr`, peers send the node's VXLAN traffic to its advertise address.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-IFACE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-IFACE**: Peers keep sending to the address a DataPathAddr interface first had

*Observed from:* underlay (outer destination address) · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Pins:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-IFACE-NAME-RESOLVED-ONCE](#SWARM-CLUSTER-IFACE-NAME-RESOLVED-ONCE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT), [SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-IFACE-NAME-RESOLVED-ONCE](#SWARM-CLUSTER-IFACE-NAME-RESOLVED-ONCE), [SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS](#SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS)

`DataPathAddr` in `POST /swarm/init` or `POST /swarm/join` names a
network interface. Peers then send the node's VXLAN traffic to the address that the interface
had when the request was made. They continue to send it to that address after the interface's
address changes, and after the daemon restarts.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS**: A Windows node's tunnel endpoint is its HNS management address, not DataPathAddr

*Observed from:* underlay · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* windows

*Needs:* [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT), [SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN) · *Narrows:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-DEFAULT](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-DEFAULT) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS), [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-IFACE](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-IFACE) · *Violates:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS)

*Applies to:* A Windows node with a task on an overlay network, whose `DataPathAddr`,
or advertise address when it has none, is not the management address (`ManagementIP`) that HNS
reports for the node's HNS network of that overlay

The node's tunnel endpoint for the network is that management address, whatever
`DataPathAddr` or the advertise address says: the other nodes send the node's VXLAN
traffic for the network to it.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-ADVERTISE-ADDRESS-IFACE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-CLUSTER-ADVERTISE-ADDRESS-IFACE**: With both given as interfaces, a manager is reached at the advertise one and VXLAN at the data-path one

*Observed from:* underlay (destination address) · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT), [SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN) · *Does not cover:* An AdvertiseAddr interface is resolved to an address once, at init or join ([SWARM-CLUSTER-ADVERTISE-IFACE-RESOLVED-ONCE](#SWARM-CLUSTER-ADVERTISE-IFACE-RESOLVED-ONCE)), A DataPathAddr interface is resolved to an address once, at init or join ([SWARM-CLUSTER-IFACE-NAME-RESOLVED-ONCE](#SWARM-CLUSTER-IFACE-NAME-RESOLVED-ONCE))

*Applies to:* A Linux node whose `POST /swarm/init` or `POST /swarm/join` named
one interface in `AdvertiseAddr` and another in `DataPathAddr`

When the node is a manager, the other nodes connect to it for Swarm management, on TCP port 2377
or the port that `AdvertiseAddr` or `ListenAddr` names, at the address of
the `AdvertiseAddr` interface. The other nodes send the node's VXLAN traffic to the
address of the `DataPathAddr` interface.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-IFACE-NAME-RESOLVED-ONCE"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-CLUSTER-IFACE-NAME-RESOLVED-ONCE**: A DataPathAddr interface is resolved to an address once, at init or join

*Observed from:* underlay (outer destination address) · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Pinned by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-IFACE](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-IFACE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT), [SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN) · *Narrows:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-ADVERTISE-ADDRESS-IFACE](#SWARM-CLUSTER-ADVERTISE-ADDRESS-IFACE), [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-IFACE](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-IFACE) · *Violates:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS)

`POST /swarm/init` and `POST /swarm/join` with `DataPathAddr` naming
a network interface replace the name with the interface's address when the request is made.
Peers keep sending the node's VXLAN traffic to that address after the interface's address
changes, and after the daemon restarts, even when no interface on the node has that address.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-ADDRESS"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-ADDRESS**: VXLAN traffic's outer source address is the one the route selects

*Observed from:* underlay (outer source address) · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Pins:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-NOT-DATA-PATH](#SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-NOT-DATA-PATH) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-NOT-DATA-PATH](#SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-NOT-DATA-PATH)

A node's VXLAN traffic to a peer has the outer source address that the node's route to that peer
selects. This holds whether or not that address is the node's data-path address.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-NOT-DATA-PATH"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-NOT-DATA-PATH**: VXLAN leaves from the routed source address, not the data-path address

*Observed from:* underlay, task, log · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Pinned by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-ADDRESS](#SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-ADDRESS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS), [SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-ADDRESS](#SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-ADDRESS) · *Violates:* [REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-CONNECTIVITY](#REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-CONNECTIVITY)

The outer source address of a node's VXLAN traffic to a peer is the address that the node's
route to that peer selects, whether or not it is the node's data-path address. When it is
another address, and no one-to-one NAT between the nodes maps it to the node's data-path
address, overlay traffic from that node does not reach the tasks on the peer, and neither node's
daemon log has an error ([moby/moby#53004](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/53004)).

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT**: DataPathPort in POST /swarm/init sets the cluster's VXLAN UDP port

*Observed from:* underlay · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT), [SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-PORT](#SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-PORT)

`DataPathPort` in `POST /swarm/init` sets the VXLAN UDP port of every Linux
node of the cluster.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-DEFAULT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-DEFAULT**: Linux and Windows nodes exchange overlay traffic on the default port

*Observed from:* task · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* Between Windows nodes, an encrypted overlay's traffic is not encrypted ([SWARM-CTR-WINDOWS-ENCRYPTION](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-CTR-WINDOWS-ENCRYPTION)) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-PORT](#SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-PORT), [SWARM-EW-WINDOWS-V6-DATA-PATH](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-EW-WINDOWS-V6-DATA-PATH)

*Applies to:* A Swarm with the default data-path port

Linux and Windows nodes in that Swarm exchange overlay traffic.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-PORT"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-PORT**: Windows nodes ignore a non-default data-path port

*Observed from:* underlay, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* windows

*Needs:* [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT), [SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN) · *Narrows:* [SWARM-WIRECLEAR-UDP-PORT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-WIRECLEAR-UDP-PORT) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT), [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-DEFAULT](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-DEFAULT) · *Violates:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT), [REQ-SWARM-DATA-PATH-VXLAN](#REQ-SWARM-DATA-PATH-VXLAN), [REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-CONNECTIVITY](#REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-CONNECTIVITY)

In a cluster with a non-default data-path port, Windows nodes do not use that port, and overlay
traffic between a task on a Windows node and a task on a Linux node does not reach its
destination.

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID-CLI**: docker swarm init refuses a data-path port outside the accepted range

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT) · *CLI form of:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A node that is not yet in a Swarm

`docker swarm init` with a data-path port outside the accepted range exits non-zero. The
node is then still not in a Swarm.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID**: POST /swarm/init refuses a data-path port outside the accepted range

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT) · *Exact form:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID-HTTP500](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID-HTTP500) · *CLI form:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID-CLI](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

or 5xx status. The node is then still not in a Swarm.

`POST /swarm/init` with a data-path port outside the accepted range responds 500.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-ZERO"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-ZERO**: A data-path port of 0 in POST /swarm/init selects 4789

*Observed from:* api:solo, api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN)
