`POST /swarm/init` with a data-path port of 0 responds 200. `GET /info` on the
node then reports 4789 as the data-path port in `Swarm.Cluster`.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOL-ALLOCATION"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOL-ALLOCATION**: An overlay without a subnet gets one of SubnetSize from DefaultAddrPool

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOLS](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOLS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-ZERO-UNALLOCATED](#SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-ZERO-UNALLOCATED)

*Applies to:* An overlay network, the ingress network included, that uses the default IPAM
driver and is created without a subnet

Once the network is allocated, as [Network lifecycle & API surface](#swarm-networking-network-lifecycle-api-surface) defines
it, `GET /networks/{id}` on a manager reports a subnet for it. That subnet is inside one
of the `DefaultAddrPool` prefixes that `GET /info` on a manager reports in
`Swarm.Cluster`. The prefix length of that subnet is the `SubnetSize` that
`GET /info` reports.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID-CLI**: docker swarm init refuses a mask length over 29 or below a pool's prefix

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOLS](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOLS) · *CLI form of:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID](#SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A node that is not yet in a Swarm

`docker swarm init` with `--default-addr-pool` exits non-zero when
`--default-addr-pool-mask-length` is greater than 29. It also exits non-zero when that
mask length is less than the prefix length of one of the pools, or is 0 and one of the pools has
a prefix longer than 24 bits. In both cases, the node is then still not in a Swarm.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID**: POST /swarm/init refuses a SubnetSize over 29 or below a pool's prefix

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOLS](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOLS) · *Exact form:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID-HTTP500](#SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID-HTTP500) · *CLI form:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID-CLI](#SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-WITHOUT-POOL-DROPPED](#SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-WITHOUT-POOL-DROPPED), [SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-ZERO-UNALLOCATED](#SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-ZERO-UNALLOCATED)

*Applies to:* A node that is not yet in a Swarm

`POST /swarm/init` with `DefaultAddrPool` set responds with a 4xx or 5xx
status when the request's `SubnetSize` is greater than 29. It also responds with a
4xx or 5xx status when the request's `SubnetSize` is less than the prefix length of
one of the pools, or is 0 and one of the pools has a prefix longer than 24 bits. In both cases,
the node is then still not in a Swarm.

`POST /swarm/init` with `DefaultAddrPool` set responds 500 when the request's

[NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Does not cover:* A container starts on a service's ingress port while no task of it runs ([SWARM-PORTALLOC-CTR-START-NO-TASK](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-PORTALLOC-CTR-START-NO-TASK)) · *Concerns:* [NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-SWARM-START-FAILS](network-common.md#NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-SWARM-START-FAILS), [SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CTR-START-REFUSED-HTTP500](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CTR-START-REFUSED-HTTP500), [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID-HTTP500](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID-HTTP500), [SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID-HTTP500](#SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID-HTTP500), [SWARM-PORTALLOC-CTR-START-HTTP500](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-PORTALLOC-CTR-START-HTTP500), [SWARM-SCOPED-NOT-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-HTTP500](#SWARM-SCOPED-NOT-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-HTTP500), [SWARM-SCOPED-NOT-ATTACHABLE-START-HTTP500](#SWARM-SCOPED-NOT-ATTACHABLE-START-HTTP500) · *Violates:* [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](network-common.md#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS)

Each request below is refused, and responds 500: (1) `POST /swarm/init` with a data-path
port outside the accepted range. (2) `POST /swarm/init` with
`DefaultAddrPool` set and a `SubnetSize` greater than 29, or with a
`SubnetSize` less than the prefix length of one of its `DefaultAddrPool`
prefixes, or of 0 with one of those prefixes longer than 24 bits. (3) `POST /containers/{id}/start` for a created or stopped container on a non-attachable Swarm-scoped
network, and `POST /networks/{id}/connect` to such a network for a running container.
(4) On a Linux node, `POST /containers/{id}/start` for a created or stopped container
that publishes a port that a service publishes in ingress mode. (5) On a node in a Swarm,
`POST /containers/{id}/start` for a created or stopped container whose network was
deleted after the container was created, or never existed.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-WITHOUT-POOL-DROPPED"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-WITHOUT-POOL-DROPPED**: Without a pool, POST /swarm/init accepts and drops SubnetSize

*Observed from:* api:solo, api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION), [SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER-DEFAULT-POOL](#SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER-DEFAULT-POOL), [SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER-DEFAULT-POOL-CLI](#SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER-DEFAULT-POOL-CLI), [SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID](#SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID) · *Violates:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOLS](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOLS)

*Applies to:* A node that is not yet in a Swarm

`POST /swarm/init` without `DefaultAddrPool` and with a
`SubnetSize` other than 0 responds 200, also when the size is greater than 29.

a prefix length of 24.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-ZERO-UNALLOCATED"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-ZERO-UNALLOCATED**: A SubnetSize of 0 with a pool is accepted and nothing is allocated

*Observed from:* api:solo, api:mgr, log · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Pinned by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-ZERO](#SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-ZERO) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOL-ALLOCATION](#SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOL-ALLOCATION), [SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID](#SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID), [SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-ZERO](#SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-ZERO) · *Violates:* [PRIN-ERRORS-ACTIONABLE](../principles.md#PRIN-ERRORS-ACTIONABLE), [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOLS](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOLS)

`POST /swarm/init` with `DefaultAddrPool` set, with no prefix longer than 24
bits, and a `SubnetSize` of 0 responds 200. No Swarm-scoped network is allocated, the
ingress network included. Only the leader manager's log reports this, in an entry that contains
`failed to create allocator`. The entry's error says that the network at index 0 `is not in canonical form`, and does not name `SubnetSize`.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER**: A manager's GET /info reports the data-path port, pool and subnet size

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOLS](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOLS), [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT) · *CLI form:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER-CLI](#SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN)

On a manager, `GET /info` includes `Swarm.Cluster`.
`Swarm.Cluster` includes the data-path port, `DefaultAddrPool` and
`SubnetSize`. When `POST /swarm/init` gave a pool, the pool is the one that
the request gave, and so is the size when the request gave a `SubnetSize` other than
0.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-GOSSIP-ADVERTISE-ADDRESS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-CLUSTER-GOSSIP-ADVERTISE-ADDRESS**: Peers send a node's gossip traffic to its advertise address

*Observed from:* underlay · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-GOSSIP-PORTS](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-GOSSIP-PORTS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-ADVERTISE-IFACE-RESOLVED-ONCE](#SWARM-CLUSTER-ADVERTISE-IFACE-RESOLVED-ONCE)

Peers send a node's gossip traffic, on TCP and UDP port 7946, to the node's advertise address.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-ADVERTISE-IFACE-RESOLVED-ONCE"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-CLUSTER-ADVERTISE-IFACE-RESOLVED-ONCE**: An AdvertiseAddr interface is resolved to an address once, at init or join

*Observed from:* underlay · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN) · *Narrows:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-ADVERTISE-ADDRESS-IFACE](#SWARM-CLUSTER-ADVERTISE-ADDRESS-IFACE) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-GOSSIP-ADVERTISE-ADDRESS](#SWARM-CLUSTER-GOSSIP-ADVERTISE-ADDRESS) · *Violates:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS)

`POST /swarm/init` and `POST /swarm/join` with `AdvertiseAddr` naming
a network interface replace the name with the interface's address when the request is made. When
the node is a manager, the other nodes keep connecting to it for Swarm management at that
address after the interface's address changes, and after the daemon restarts, even when no
interface on the node has that address. Peers also keep sending the node's gossip traffic to
that address.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-GOSSIP-LISTEN-ADDRESS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-CLUSTER-GOSSIP-LISTEN-ADDRESS**: A node listens for gossip on port 7946 at its listen address's host

*Observed from:* node · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-GOSSIP-PORTS](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-GOSSIP-PORTS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN)

A node listens for gossip on TCP and UDP port 7946, on the host part of its listen address.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-GOSSIP-NO-CLEARTEXT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-CLUSTER-GOSSIP-NO-CLEARTEXT**: Gossip traffic shows no network IDs, service names or task addresses

*Observed from:* underlay · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-CONTROL-ENCRYPTED](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-CONTROL-ENCRYPTED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

*Applies to:* An overlay network, and a service on it whose tasks run on two nodes

A capture of the gossip traffic between the two nodes, on TCP and UDP port 7946, taken from
before the service is created until each task resolves the name of the task on the other node,
does not contain the network's ID, the service's name or the tasks' addresses on the network.
Each is searched for in the text form that the API reports, an address without its prefix
length. Every UDP datagram and every message on a TCP connection in the capture is encrypted:
without the Swarm's gossip keys, none of them decodes as one of memberlist's unencrypted
messages. This holds whether or not the network is `encrypted`.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-MANAGEMENT-NO-CLEARTEXT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-CLUSTER-MANAGEMENT-NO-CLEARTEXT**: Management traffic to a manager carries only TLS

*Observed from:* underlay · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-CONTROL-ENCRYPTED](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-CONTROL-ENCRYPTED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A Swarm with one manager, and a node that is not in a Swarm

`POST /swarm/join` on the node, with the Swarm's worker join token and the manager's
address in `RemoteAddrs`, responds 200, and `POST /swarm/leave` on the node
then responds 200. A capture of the TCP traffic between the node and the manager, on the port
that `RemoteAddrs` names, taken from before the join is sent until the leave
responds, carries only TLS records on every connection. It does not contain the node's name as
`GET /info` on the node reports it in `Name`.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-V6"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-V6**: An IPv6 DataPathAddr produces IPv6 outer packets for overlay traffic

*Observed from:* underlay · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS](#REQ-SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPV6](#SWARM-HOST-IPV6), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT), [SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-MIXED-VERSIONS-ACCEPTED](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-MIXED-VERSIONS-ACCEPTED), [SWARM-EW-WINDOWS-V6-DATA-PATH](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-EW-WINDOWS-V6-DATA-PATH)

An IPv6 `DataPathAddr` in `POST /swarm/init` or `POST /swarm/join`
produces IPv6 outer packets for overlay traffic.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-MIXED-VERSION"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-MIXED-VERSION**: A join with a data-path address of the other IP version succeeds

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Pins:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-MIXED-VERSIONS-ACCEPTED](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-MIXED-VERSIONS-ACCEPTED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPV6](#SWARM-HOST-IPV6), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-MIXED-VERSIONS-ACCEPTED](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-MIXED-VERSIONS-ACCEPTED)

*Applies to:* A Swarm whose nodes have data-path addresses of one IP version

`POST /swarm/join` to that Swarm with a data-path address of the other IP version
responds 200. The node is then in the Swarm.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-MIXED-VERSIONS-ACCEPTED"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-MIXED-VERSIONS-ACCEPTED**: A join with a data-path address of the other IP version is accepted

*Observed from:* api:solo, task, log · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Pinned by:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-MIXED-VERSION](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-MIXED-VERSION) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPV6](#SWARM-HOST-IPV6), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT), [SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REJOIN) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-MIXED-VERSION](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-MIXED-VERSION), [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-V6](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-V6) · *Violates:* [REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-CONNECTIVITY](#REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-CONNECTIVITY)

`POST /swarm/join` with a `DataPathAddr` of a different IP version from the
data-path addresses of the Swarm's other nodes responds 200. Overlay traffic between two nodes
whose data-path addresses have different IP versions does not reach its destination. Only the
daemon log of each of the two nodes reports the failure to program the other node as a peer
([*SWARM-FAILREP-PEER*](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-FAILREP-PEER)).

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-LIVE-RESTORE-RELOAD**: A reload that turns on live-restore on a node in a Swarm is accepted

*Observed from:* api:mgr, api:wkr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Rationale:* Live-restore on a node in a Swarm changes what a daemon restart does to its tasks ([RAT-SWARM-LIVE-RESTORE-REFUSED](#RAT-SWARM-LIVE-RESTORE-REFUSED))

*Applies to:* A Linux node in a Swarm, with `live-restore` false

The daemon's `daemon.json` is changed to set `live-restore` to true, and the
daemon receives `SIGHUP`. `GET /info` then reports
`LiveRestoreEnabled` as true and `Swarm.LocalNodeState` as `active`.

<a id="swarm-networking-network-lifecycle-api-surface"></a>

## Network lifecycle & API surface

A Swarm-scoped network is a network that the Swarm managers keep. Its driver is a multi-host driver
or a node-local driver. A multi-host driver is `overlay`, or a driver of a managed plugin
that reports the scope `global` in its capabilities. A node-local driver is `bridge`,
`host`, `ipvlan`, `macvlan`, or a driver of a managed plugin that reports
the scope `local`. A network of a node-local driver is Swarm-scoped when it is created with
`Scope` set to `swarm` (`--scope swarm`). A manager accepts as the node-local
driver of a Swarm-scoped network only `bridge`, `host`, `ipvlan`,
`macvlan` or a driver that a managed plugin provides. Windows nodes have none of these
drivers, so the expectations about a Swarm-scoped network of a node-local driver hold on Linux
nodes.

A Swarm-scoped network is allocated after the network is created, and asynchronously. In this spec,
a network is allocated once `GET /networks/{id}` on a manager reports the network's
`Driver`.

<a id="swarm-networking-overlay-driver-options"></a>

### Overlay driver options

An expectation in this section that refers to other expectations or to another section states that
`POST /networks/create` for an overlay network with the option responds 201, and that the
network then shows the behavior that the option selects, in the observable that the expectation
names. Its *Observed from* and *Depends on* fields cover that observable. The expectations or the
section that it refers to specify the behavior in full, and what it depends on.

<a id="SWARM-OVLOPT-MTU"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-OVLOPT-MTU**: The mtu option sets the base MTU before encapsulation overhead

*Observed from:* api:mgr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux · *Key:* `com.docker.network.driver.mtu`

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-DRIVER-OPTIONS](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-DRIVER-OPTIONS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-CTR-WINDOWS-MTU-OPTION](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-CTR-WINDOWS-MTU-OPTION), [SWARM-OVL-MTU-UNCHECKED](#SWARM-OVL-MTU-UNCHECKED)

The option sets the base MTU from which encapsulation overhead is subtracted. `POST /networks/create` for an overlay network with the option responds 201, and a task on the network
observes the inner MTU that these expectations compute from the option's value as the base:
[*SWARM-CTR-MTU-CLEARTEXT*](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-CTR-MTU-CLEARTEXT), [*SWARM-CTR-MTU-CLEARTEXT-V6*](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-CTR-MTU-CLEARTEXT-V6),
[*SWARM-CTR-MTU-ENCRYPTED*](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-CTR-MTU-ENCRYPTED) and [*SWARM-CTR-MTU-ENCRYPTED-V6*](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-CTR-MTU-ENCRYPTED-V6).

<a id="SWARM-OVLOPT-MTU-WINDOWS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-OVLOPT-MTU-WINDOWS**: Windows nodes run tasks on a network with the mtu option set

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* windows · *Key:* `com.docker.network.driver.mtu`

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-API-BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE](network-common.md#REQ-NET-API-BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE) · *Needs:* [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-CTR-WINDOWS-MTU-OPTION](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-CTR-WINDOWS-MTU-OPTION)

A task on a network with this option set runs on a Windows node.

<a id="SWARM-OVLOPT-VNI-LIST"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-OVLOPT-VNI-LIST**: The vxlanid_list option sets one VNI per IPAM subnet

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux · *Key:* `com.docker.network.driver.overlay.vxlanid_list`

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-VNI-LIST](#REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-VNI-LIST), [REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-VNI-REPORTED](#REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-VNI-REPORTED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION)

The option sets the network's VNIs, one per IPAM subnet. `POST /networks/create` for an
overlay network whose option lists as many VNIs as the network has subnets responds 201. Once
the network is allocated, `GET /networks/{id}` on a manager reports those VNIs in
`vxlanid_list`, in the order of the network's subnets. See [*SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST*](#SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST).

<a id="SWARM-OVLOPT-ENCRYPTED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-OVLOPT-ENCRYPTED**: The encrypted option selects an encrypted overlay

*Observed from:* api:mgr, underlay · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux · *Key:* `encrypted`

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-DRIVER-OPTIONS](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-DRIVER-OPTIONS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-ENC-MATCHES](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-ENC-MATCHES), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-MANGLE-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-MANGLE-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-ROUTE-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-ROUTE-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN), [SWARM-HOST-XFRM](#SWARM-HOST-XFRM) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-CTR-WINDOWS-ENCRYPTION](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-CTR-WINDOWS-ENCRYPTION)

The option selects an encrypted overlay, which [Encryption](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-encryption) in
[swarm-lifecycle.md](swarm-lifecycle.md) specifies. `POST /networks/create` for an
overlay network with the option responds 201, and the traffic between nodes for the network's
VNI is IPsec ESP, as [*SWARM-ENC-ESP*](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-ENC-ESP) states.

<a id="SWARM-OVLOPT-DSR"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-OVLOPT-DSR**: The dsr option selects direct server return for east-west VIP traffic

*Observed from:* api:mgr, task · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux · *Key:* `dsr`

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-DRIVER-OPTIONS](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-DRIVER-OPTIONS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LB-EXTENSIONS](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LB-EXTENSIONS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-MANGLE-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-MANGLE-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPVS](#SWARM-HOST-IPVS), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#SWARM-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [SWARM-HOST-NFT-NETDEV-EGRESS-COMMAND](#SWARM-HOST-NFT-NETDEV-EGRESS-COMMAND), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-NETDEV](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-NETDEV), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-LB-WINDOWS-DSR](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-LB-WINDOWS-DSR)

The option selects direct server return for east-west VIP traffic on Linux nodes. `POST /networks/create` for an overlay network with the option responds 201, and a task that receives
VIP traffic on the network observes the client's real source address, as
[*SWARM-LB-DSR-SOURCE*](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-LB-DSR-SOURCE) states. See also [*SWARM-LB-DSR-DESTINATION*](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-LB-DSR-DESTINATION).

<a id="SWARM-OVLOPT-DSR-WINDOWS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-OVLOPT-DSR-WINDOWS**: Windows nodes run tasks on a network with the dsr option set

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* windows · *Key:* `dsr`

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-API-BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE](network-common.md#REQ-NET-API-BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE) · *Needs:* [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-LB-WINDOWS-DSR](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-LB-WINDOWS-DSR)

A task on a network with this option set runs on a Windows node.

<a id="SWARM-OVLOPT-FLAG-ANY-VALUE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-OVLOPT-FLAG-ANY-VALUE**: On Linux, encrypted and dsr take effect whatever their value

*Observed from:* api:mgr, underlay, task · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux · *Key:* `encrypted`, `dsr`

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-DRIVER-OPTIONS](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-DRIVER-OPTIONS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-ENC-MATCHES](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-ENC-MATCHES), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LB-EXTENSIONS](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LB-EXTENSIONS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-MANGLE-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-MANGLE-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-ROUTE-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-ROUTE-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPVS](#SWARM-HOST-IPVS), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#SWARM-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [SWARM-HOST-NFT-NETDEV-EGRESS-COMMAND](#SWARM-HOST-NFT-NETDEV-EGRESS-COMMAND), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-NETDEV](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-NETDEV), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN), [SWARM-HOST-XFRM](#SWARM-HOST-XFRM) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

On Linux nodes, each key takes effect when it is present in the network's options, whatever its
value. This includes the empty string and `false` as values: with either value, a network
created with `encrypted` shows the observable that [*SWARM-OVLOPT-ENCRYPTED*](#SWARM-OVLOPT-ENCRYPTED) names,
and one created with `dsr` shows the observable that [*SWARM-OVLOPT-DSR*](#SWARM-OVLOPT-DSR) names.

<a id="swarm-networking-swarm-scoped-networks"></a>

### Swarm-scoped networks

The expectations in this subsection hold for any Swarm-scoped network, whatever its driver. An
expectation here about a network that is not Swarm-scoped and that has the name of a Swarm-scoped
network does not cover the Swarm's predefined networks, whose names are those of the node's own
`bridge` and `host` networks.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE**: A manager creates a network with Scope swarm or a multi-host driver

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-CONFIG-FROM](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-CONFIG-FROM), [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-CREATE-ON-MANAGER](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-CREATE-ON-MANAGER), [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-PLUGIN-DRIVERS](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-PLUGIN-DRIVERS) · *CLI form:* [SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Does not cover:* A plugin network is allocated only while the leader has the plugin ([SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-ON-LEADER](#SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-ON-LEADER)), A plugin named without its tag responds 500 or is never allocated ([SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-UNTAGGED-NAME](#SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-UNTAGGED-NAME))

*Applies to:* A manager, and the `bridge`, `ipvlan`, `macvlan` or
`overlay` driver, or a driver that a managed plugin provides

On that manager, `POST /networks/create` that sets no fields other than
`Name`, `Driver` and `Scope`, with a name that no Swarm-scoped
network has and no network on that manager has, responds 201 when it sets `Scope` to
`swarm`, or when it names a multi-host driver, such as `overlay`, and does not set
`Scope` to `local`. `GET /networks` on a manager then lists the network.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-CLI**: docker network create --scope=swarm or --driver overlay makes a network

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-CREATE-ON-MANAGER](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-CREATE-ON-MANAGER) · *CLI form of:* [SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE](#SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A manager

On that manager, `docker network create --scope=swarm` with a name that no Swarm-scoped
network has, and no network on that manager has, exits zero. `docker network create --driver overlay` with such a name, in place of the first command, also exits zero. `docker network ls` on a manager then lists the network.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-LOCAL-SCOPE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-LOCAL-SCOPE**: A manager refuses a multi-host driver with Scope local

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED), [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](network-common.md#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS) · *Exact form:* [SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-LOCAL-SCOPE-HTTP403](#SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-LOCAL-SCOPE-HTTP403) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A manager, and a name that no network has

On that manager, `POST /networks/create` with that name, a multi-host driver, such as
`overlay`, and `Scope` set to `local` responds with a 4xx status.
`GET /networks` on a manager then lists no network with that name.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-LOCAL-SCOPE-HTTP403"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-LOCAL-SCOPE-HTTP403**: A multi-host driver with Scope local responds 403

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Exact form of:* [SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-LOCAL-SCOPE](#SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-LOCAL-SCOPE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A manager

On that manager, `POST /networks/create` with a multi-host driver, such as
`overlay`, and `Scope` set to `local` responds 403, with a message that
contains `cannot downgrade network scope for`.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-ALLOCATED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-ALLOCATED**: A Swarm-scoped network reports its Driver within the allocation ceiling

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-CREATE-ON-MANAGER](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-CREATE-ON-MANAGER) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-OVL-ALLOCATION-FAILURE-UNREPORTED](#SWARM-OVL-ALLOCATION-FAILURE-UNREPORTED)

Within the [*allocation ceiling (30 s)*](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION) after
`POST /networks/create` for a Swarm-scoped network responds 201, `GET /networks/{id}` on a manager reports the network's `Driver`.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-WORKER-OVERLAY-CREATE-ERROR"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-SCOPED-WORKER-OVERLAY-CREATE-ERROR**: An overlay create on a worker says to join a Swarm

*Observed from:* api:wkr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-WORKER](#SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-WORKER) · *Violates:* [PRIN-ERRORS-ACTIONABLE](../principles.md#PRIN-ERRORS-ACTIONABLE)

On a worker, `POST /networks/create` with `Driver` set to `overlay`
responds with an error whose message is `This node is not a swarm manager. Use "docker swarm init" or "docker swarm join" to connect this node to swarm and try again.` The
message tells a node that is already in a Swarm to join a Swarm.

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-DELETE](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-DELETE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-DELETE-NOT-FOUND"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-DELETE-NOT-FOUND**: Deleting the Swarm's bridge or host network by its ID responds 404

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Narrows:* [SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-SERVICE](#SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-SERVICE), [SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-SERVICE-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-SERVICE-CLI), [SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-SERVICE-MSG](#SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-SERVICE-MSG), [SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-TASK](#SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-TASK), [SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-TASK-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-TASK-CLI), [SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-TASK-MSG](#SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-TASK-MSG) · *Concerns:* [NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED](network-common.md#NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED), [NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED-CLI](network-common.md#NET-API-DELETE-PREDEFINED-CLI) · *Violates:* [REQ-NET-LOOKUP](network-common.md#REQ-NET-LOOKUP), [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-DELETE-IN-USE](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-DELETE-IN-USE)

On a manager, `DELETE /networks/{id}` with the full ID of one of the Swarm's predefined
networks, or with a prefix of that ID that the ID of no other network starts with and that is
not a network name, responds 404, with a message that contains `not found`. This
holds whether or not a service refers to the network. `GET /networks/{id}` with that ID
then still responds 200 with the network.

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-LOCAL**: A worker creates a local network with a Swarm-scoped network's name

*Observed from:* api:mgr, api:wkr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Pinned by:* [SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-AMBIGUOUS-HTTP400](#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-AMBIGUOUS-HTTP400), [SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-START-BY-ID](#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-START-BY-ID), [SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-START-BY-NAME](#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-START-BY-NAME), [SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-TASKS](#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-TASKS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Narrows:* [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT), [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-CLI), [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START), [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-CLI), [SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-CONFLICT](#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-CONFLICT) · *Concerns:* [NET-API-INSPECT-ID-NAME-PREFIX](network-common.md#NET-API-INSPECT-ID-NAME-PREFIX), [NET-API-INSPECT-ID-NAME-PREFIX-CLI](network-common.md#NET-API-INSPECT-ID-NAME-PREFIX-CLI), [SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-AMBIGUOUS](#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-AMBIGUOUS), [SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-START-BY-ID](#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-START-BY-ID), [SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-START-BY-NAME](#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-START-BY-NAME), [SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-TASKS](#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-TASKS) · *Violates:* [REQ-NET-NAME-UNIQUE](network-common.md#REQ-NET-NAME-UNIQUE), [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-WORKER-ON-DEMAND](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-WORKER-ON-DEMAND)

`POST /networks/create` on a worker, for a network that is not Swarm-scoped and that has
the name of a Swarm-scoped network other than one of the Swarm's predefined networks, responds
201. The same request responds 409 on a manager. `POST /nodes/{id}/update` that sets the
`Role` of a worker that has such a network to `manager` responds 200, and
`GET /nodes/{id}` then reports `manager` as the node's `Spec.Role`. On a
manager with both networks, `GET /networks/{id}` and `DELETE /networks/{id}`
with the shared name respond with a 4xx or 5xx status. On any node with both networks, the node
rejects the Swarm-scoped network's tasks, `POST /containers/{id}/start` for a standalone
container that names the Swarm-scoped network by its ID fails, and one that names it by its name
is attached to the other network. `POST /networks/{id}/connect` for a running container
there fails when `{id}` is the Swarm-scoped network's ID, and attaches the container to the
other network when `{id}` is the shared name.

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-SCOPED-INSPECT**: GET /networks/{id} reports Scope swarm and the network's create fields

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-NET-INSPECT-CONFIGURATION](network-common.md#REQ-NET-INSPECT-CONFIGURATION), [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-SCOPE-VISIBLE](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-SCOPE-VISIBLE) · *CLI form:* [SWARM-SCOPED-INSPECT-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-INSPECT-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION)

Once a Swarm-scoped network is allocated, `GET /networks/{id}` for that network reports
`Scope` as `swarm`, and reports `Created`. It also reports the
`Driver`, `Ingress`, `Attachable`, `Internal`,
`EnableIPv6`, `ConfigFrom` and `Labels` given at create. For an
overlay network, it also reports the `IPAM` of the allocation.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-DANGLING"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-DANGLING**: dangling=true lists every Swarm-scoped network, and false attached ones

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Pins:* [NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-SWARM-SCOPED](network-common.md#NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-SWARM-SCOPED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Concerned by:* [NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-SWARM-SCOPED](network-common.md#NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-SWARM-SCOPED)

*Applies to:* A manager

`GET /networks` with the filter `dangling=true` lists every Swarm-scoped
network other than the Swarm's predefined networks, including the ingress network and networks
that services use. `GET /networks` with the filter `dangling=false` lists the
Swarm-scoped networks that have a local attachment on that manager. Those networks are then in
both responses.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-MANAGER"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-MANAGER**: A manager lists each Swarm-scoped network with Scope swarm

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-SCOPE-VISIBLE](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-SCOPE-VISIBLE) · *CLI form:* [SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-MANAGER-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-MANAGER-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

`GET /networks` on a manager lists each Swarm-scoped network other than the Swarm's
predefined networks, and reports its `Scope` as `swarm`. This holds whether or not
the manager has a local attachment to the network.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-MANAGER-CLI"></a>

`docker network ls` on a manager lists each Swarm-scoped network other than the Swarm's
predefined networks.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-SCOPE-FILTER"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-SCOPE-FILTER**: The scope filter lists only the networks of that scope

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-SCOPE-VISIBLE](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-SCOPE-VISIBLE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A manager, a Swarm-scoped network other than one of the Swarm's predefined
networks, and a network whose `Scope` is `local`

On that manager, `GET /networks` with the filter `scope=swarm` lists the
Swarm-scoped network and not the other one. With the filter `scope=local`, it lists
the other one and not the Swarm-scoped network.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-NOT-LISTED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-NOT-LISTED**: On a manager, GET /networks never lists the Swarm's bridge or host network

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Rationale:* The Swarm's bridge and host networks stand for each node's own network ([RAT-SWARM-PREDEFINED-NETWORKS](#RAT-SWARM-PREDEFINED-NETWORKS))

On a manager, `GET /networks` does not list the Swarm's predefined networks, with or
without filters. This includes the filters `scope=swarm`, `type=builtin`,
`type=custom` and `dangling=true`, and an `id` filter with the
full ID of one of them.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-INSPECT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-INSPECT**: The Swarm's bridge and host networks are found by ID, prefix or scope=swarm

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Rationale:* The Swarm's bridge and host networks stand for each node's own network ([RAT-SWARM-PREDEFINED-NETWORKS](#RAT-SWARM-PREDEFINED-NETWORKS))

On a manager, `GET /networks/{id}` responds 200 with one of the Swarm's predefined
networks when `{id}` is its full ID, or a prefix of its ID that the ID of no other network
starts with and that is not a network name. It does the same when `{id}` is `bridge`
or `host` and `scope` is `swarm`. The response reports the
`Name` `bridge` or `host`, a `Driver` of the same name,
`Scope` `swarm`, an empty `IPAM.Config`, and
`com.docker.swarm.predefined` set to `true` in `Labels`.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START**: A container on an attachable network starts on any active node

*Observed from:* api:active · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-ATTACHABLE](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-ATTACHABLE) · *CLI form:* [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Does not cover:* After an attachment times out, the next request skips the attachment ([SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-RETRY-SKIPS-ATTACHMENT](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-RETRY-SKIPS-ATTACHMENT)), A container naming an attachable network by ID prefix fails with 500 ([SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-ID-PREFIX](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-ID-PREFIX)), A worker creates a local network with a Swarm-scoped network's name ([SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-LOCAL](#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-LOCAL)), A container naming the Swarm network by ID fails to start with 500 ([SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-START-BY-ID](#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-START-BY-ID)) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-STANDALONE-ATTACH](#SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-STANDALONE-ATTACH)

On any node whose availability is `active`, `POST /containers/{id}/start` for a
created or stopped container on an attachable Swarm-scoped network, with no static address on
that network or with static addresses that are inside the network's subnets and not in use on
the network, responds 204. The container is then running and has an address on the network. For
a network created with `ConfigFrom`, this holds for a network of a node-local driver,
on a node that has the config-only network that `ConfigFrom` names. For a network
whose driver is a managed plugin, this holds on a node that has that plugin enabled.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-CLI**: docker run on an attachable network succeeds on any active node

*Observed from:* api:active · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-ATTACHABLE](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-ATTACHABLE) · *CLI form of:* [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Does not cover:* A container naming an attachable network by ID prefix fails with 500 ([SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-ID-PREFIX](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-ID-PREFIX)), A worker creates a local network with a Swarm-scoped network's name ([SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-LOCAL](#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-LOCAL)), A container naming the Swarm network by ID fails to start with 500 ([SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-START-BY-ID](#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-START-BY-ID))

On any node whose availability is `active`, `docker run -d --network` naming an
attachable Swarm-scoped network exits zero. The container then runs and is attached to the
network. For a network created with `ConfigFrom`, this holds for a network of a
node-local driver, on a node that has the config-only network that `ConfigFrom`
names. For a network whose driver is a managed plugin, this holds on a node that has that plugin
enabled.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-ID-PREFIX"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-ID-PREFIX**: A container naming an attachable network by ID prefix fails with 500

*Observed from:* api:active · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Narrows:* [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START), [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-CLI) · *Violates:* [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](network-common.md#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS), [REQ-NET-LOOKUP](network-common.md#REQ-NET-LOOKUP)

*Applies to:* An attachable Swarm-scoped network, a prefix of its ID, shorter than the ID, that
the ID of no other network starts with and that is not a network name, and a created or stopped
standalone container that names the network by that prefix

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds 500, with a message that
contains `network <prefix> not found`, where `<prefix>` is that prefix.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT**: A running container connects to an attachable network on any active node

*Observed from:* api:active · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-ATTACHABLE](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-ATTACHABLE) · *CLI form:* [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Does not cover:* After an attachment times out, the next request skips the attachment ([SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-RETRY-SKIPS-ATTACHMENT](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-RETRY-SKIPS-ATTACHMENT)), Connecting by an attachable network's ID prefix fails with 500 ([SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-ID-PREFIX](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-ID-PREFIX)), A worker creates a local network with a Swarm-scoped network's name ([SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-LOCAL](#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-LOCAL)) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-STANDALONE-ATTACH](#SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-STANDALONE-ATTACH)

On any node whose availability is `active`, `POST /networks/{id}/connect` to an
attachable Swarm-scoped network, for a running standalone container that is not attached to the
network, with no address in `EndpointConfig.IPAMConfig` or with addresses there that
are inside the network's subnets and not in use on the network, responds 200. The container then
has an address on the network. For a network created with `ConfigFrom`, this holds
for a network of a node-local driver, on a node that has the config-only network that
`ConfigFrom` names. For a network whose driver is a managed plugin, this holds on a
node that has that plugin enabled.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-CLI**: docker network connect to an attachable network succeeds on active nodes

*Observed from:* api:active · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-ATTACHABLE](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-ATTACHABLE) · *CLI form of:* [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Does not cover:* After an attachment times out, the next request skips the attachment ([SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-RETRY-SKIPS-ATTACHMENT](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-RETRY-SKIPS-ATTACHMENT)), Connecting by an attachable network's ID prefix fails with 500 ([SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-ID-PREFIX](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-ID-PREFIX)), A worker creates a local network with a Swarm-scoped network's name ([SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-LOCAL](#SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-LOCAL))

On any node whose availability is `active`, `docker network connect` naming an attachable
Swarm-scoped network and a running standalone container that is not attached to it, without
`--ip` and `--ip6` or with addresses in them that are inside the network's
subnets and not in use on the network, exits zero. The container then has an address on the
network. For a network created with `ConfigFrom`, this holds for a network of a
node-local driver, on a node that has the config-only network that `ConfigFrom`
names. For a network whose driver is a managed plugin, this holds on a node that has that plugin
enabled.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-ID-PREFIX"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-ID-PREFIX**: Connecting by an attachable network's ID prefix fails with 500

*Observed from:* api:active · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Narrows:* [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT), [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-CLI) · *Violates:* [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](network-common.md#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS), [REQ-NET-LOOKUP](network-common.md#REQ-NET-LOOKUP)

*Applies to:* An attachable Swarm-scoped network, a prefix of its ID, shorter than the ID, that
the ID of no other network starts with and that is not a network name, and a running standalone
container that is not attached to the network

`POST /networks/{id}/connect` with that prefix as `{id}`, for the container, responds
500, with a message that contains `network <prefix> not found`, where `<prefix>` is
that prefix. `GET /containers/{id}/json` then does not list the network in
`NetworkSettings.Networks`.

*Refines:* [PRIN-ERRORS-ACTIONABLE](../principles.md#PRIN-ERRORS-ACTIONABLE), [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-CONFIG-FROM](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-CONFIG-FROM), [REQ-SWARM-TASK-ERRORS](#REQ-SWARM-TASK-ERRORS) · *Exact form:* [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-TASKS-MSG](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-TASKS-MSG) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)
