<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-FAILURE-TIMEOUT"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-FAILURE-TIMEOUT**: Attachment failures for standalone containers time out

*Observed from:* api:mgr, api:wkr, log · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Pinned by:* [SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CTR-START-REFUSED-HTTP500](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CTR-START-REFUSED-HTTP500), [SWARM-ENC-NO-XFRM-CTR-START-HTTP500](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-ENC-NO-XFRM-CTR-START-HTTP500), [SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-IN-USE-HTTP500](#SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-IN-USE-HTTP500), [SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-UNATTACHED](#SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-UNATTACHED), [SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-CTR-START-HTTP500](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-CTR-START-HTTP500), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-CONNECT-HTTP500](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-CONNECT-HTTP500), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-START-HTTP500](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-START-HTTP500), [SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-CONNECT-HTTP500](#SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-CONNECT-HTTP500), [SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-START-HTTP500](#SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-START-HTTP500) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Does not cover:* After an attachment times out, the next request skips the attachment ([SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-RETRY-SKIPS-ATTACHMENT](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-RETRY-SKIPS-ATTACHMENT)) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CTR-START](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CTR-START), [SWARM-ENC-NO-XFRM-CTR-START](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-ENC-NO-XFRM-CTR-START), [SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-IN-USE](#SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-IN-USE), [SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-ATTACHED](#SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE-ATTACHED), [SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-CTR-START](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-CTR-START), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-CONNECT](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-CONNECT), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-START](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-START), [SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-CONNECT](#SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-CONNECT), [SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-START](#SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-START) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-SCOPED-HOST-DRIVER-UNUSABLE](#SWARM-SCOPED-HOST-DRIVER-UNUSABLE) · *Violates:* [PRIN-ERRORS-ACTIONABLE](../principles.md#PRIN-ERRORS-ACTIONABLE), [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](network-common.md#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS)

If the attachment of a standalone container to an attachable network fails, `POST /containers/{id}/start` waits 20 seconds. It then responds 500 with `attaching to network failed, make sure your network options are correct and check manager logs: context deadline exceeded`. This occurs in nine cases: (1) On a Linux node, the network is
`encrypted`, and the host's kernel does not offer the XFRM netlink interface. (2) The
network is an overlay network created with `ConfigFrom`. (3) The network is deleted
after the request has found it, but before the attachment task is created. (4) The container's
static address is in use or is outside the network's subnets. (5) The network is not allocated.
(6) The container's node has availability `drain` or `pause`. (7) The network is a
Swarm-scoped network of a node-local driver created with `ConfigFrom`, and the
container's node does not have the config-only network that `ConfigFrom` names. (8)
The network is a Swarm-scoped network of the `host` driver. (9) The network's driver is
a managed plugin that the container's node does not have enabled. `POST /networks/{id}/connect` for a running container also waits 20 seconds in each of these cases,
and then responds 500 with the same message. In cases 1, 2, 7 and 8, while the request waits,
`GET /tasks` with the `runtime=attachment` filter lists the attachment task
as rejected, and its `Status.Err` contains the error that a service's task gets for
the same cause: `cannot join secure network: required modules to install IPSEC rules are missing on host` in case 1, `user-specified configurations are not supported if the network depends on a configuration network` in case 2, `configuration network "<name>" does not exist` in case 7, and `only one instance of "host" network is allowed` in case 8. The task is deleted before the request responds. After that, that error is
only in the node's daemon log, in an entry at the error level that contains it. In case 3, the
attachment task is deleted, and no manager's daemon log reports the failure. In cases 4 and 5,
the attachment task stays in the `new` state until it is deleted. `GET /tasks` reports
that state. The reason then appears only in the leader manager's log, in an entry that contains
`task allocation failure`. In cases 6 and 9, the attachment task stays in the `pending`
state until it is deleted. `GET /tasks` reports that state.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-HOST-DRIVER-UNUSABLE"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-SCOPED-HOST-DRIVER-UNUSABLE**: A Swarm-scoped host network is created, and every attachment fails

*Observed from:* api:mgr, api:active · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-FAILURE-TIMEOUT](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-FAILURE-TIMEOUT) · *Violates:* [PRIN-FAIL-FAST](../principles.md#PRIN-FAIL-FAST)

`POST /networks/create` on a manager for a Swarm-scoped network whose
`Driver` is `host` responds 201. Every attachment to the network then fails,
on every node. The tasks of a service on the network are rejected, and their error in
`GET /tasks` contains `only one instance of "host" network is allowed`. When
the network is attachable, `POST /containers/{id}/start` for a standalone container on
the network, and `POST /networks/{id}/connect` to the network for a running container,
fail as [*SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-FAILURE-TIMEOUT*](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-FAILURE-TIMEOUT) states.

*Observed from:* api:mgr, api:wkr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Narrows:* [SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CTR-START-REFUSED-HTTP500](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CHURN-DELETE-CTR-START-REFUSED-HTTP500), [SWARM-ENC-NO-XFRM-CTR-START-HTTP500](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-ENC-NO-XFRM-CTR-START-HTTP500), [SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-IN-USE-HTTP500](#SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-IN-USE-HTTP500), [SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-CTR-START-HTTP500](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-CTR-START-HTTP500), [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-FAILURE-TIMEOUT](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-FAILURE-TIMEOUT), [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT), [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-CLI), [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-CONNECT-HTTP500](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-CONNECT-HTTP500), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-START-HTTP500](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MISSING-START-HTTP500), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-OVERLAY-UNUSABLE](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-OVERLAY-UNUSABLE), [SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-CONNECT](#SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-CONNECT), [SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-CONNECT-HTTP500](#SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-CONNECT-HTTP500), [SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-STANDALONE-ATTACH](#SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-STANDALONE-ATTACH), [SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-START-HTTP500](#SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-START-HTTP500) · *Violates:* [PRIN-REPEATABLE](../principles.md#PRIN-REPEATABLE), [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-ATTACHABLE](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-ATTACHABLE)

*Applies to:* A standalone container, an attachable Swarm-scoped network and a node, where the
container's last `POST /containers/{id}/start` on the node, or its last `POST /networks/{id}/connect` to the network on the node, responded 500 after 20 seconds with
`attaching to network failed, make sure your network options are correct and check manager logs: context deadline exceeded`

The next such request on that node, a start of the container or a connect of the container that
names the network as the timed-out connect did, does not wait for an attachment where the node
has no local attachment to the network, whatever the node's availability. It responds 404 at
once, with a message that contains `network <ref> not found`. For a start, `<ref>`
is the network's full ID if the container has been started before, and otherwise the network
name or ID that the container was created with. For a connect, it is the `{id}` of the
request. Where the node has a local attachment to the network, the next such connect responds
200 at once. `GET /containers/{id}/json` then lists the network in
`NetworkSettings.Networks`, and `GET /tasks` on a manager with the
`runtime=attachment` filter lists no attachment task for the container. On a node
whose availability is still `drain` or `pause`, that connect responds 200 where the same
request in the same state responded 500.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-OVERLAY-UNUSABLE"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-OVERLAY-UNUSABLE**: An overlay with ConfigFrom is created, and every attachment fails

*Observed from:* api:mgr, api:active · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Pinned by:* [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-OVERLAY](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-OVERLAY) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Does not cover:* After an attachment times out, the next request skips the attachment ([SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-RETRY-SKIPS-ATTACHMENT](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-RETRY-SKIPS-ATTACHMENT)) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-OVERLAY](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-OVERLAY), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-TASKS](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-TASKS) · *Violates:* [PRIN-ERRORS-ACTIONABLE](../principles.md#PRIN-ERRORS-ACTIONABLE), [REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS](network-common.md#REQ-NET-API-ERROR-STATUS), [REQ-NET-CONFIG-FROM](network-common.md#REQ-NET-CONFIG-FROM)

`POST /networks/create` for an overlay network with `ConfigFrom` responds 201
only if the config-only network exists on the manager that handles the request. It responds 404
otherwise. Every attachment to the network then fails. The tasks of a service on the network are
rejected, and their error in `GET /tasks` contains `user-specified configurations are not supported if the network depends on a configuration network`. When the
network is attachable, `POST /containers/{id}/start` for a standalone container on the
network responds 500 after 20 seconds, with a message that contains `attaching to network failed, make sure your network options are correct and check manager logs: context deadline exceeded`.

*CLI form of:* [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-CREATE-MISSING](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-CREATE-MISSING) · *Pins:* [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-ONLY-ONE-NODE](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-ONLY-ONE-NODE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A manager that does not have a given config-only network

On that manager, `docker network create --scope=swarm --config-from` naming that network
exits non-zero and prints the daemon's error. So does `docker network create --driver overlay --config-from` naming that network.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-ONLY-ONE-NODE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-ONLY-ONE-NODE**: ConfigFrom is checked only on the manager that handles the create

*Observed from:* api:mgr, api:active · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Pinned by:* [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-CREATE-MISSING](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-CREATE-MISSING), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-CREATE-MISSING-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-CREATE-MISSING-CLI), [SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MANAGER-ONLY](#SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-MANAGER-ONLY) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Rationale:* The managers do not track which nodes have a config-only network ([RAT-SWARM-CONFIG-ONLY-PER-NODE](#RAT-SWARM-CONFIG-ONLY-PER-NODE))

`POST /networks/create` for a Swarm-scoped network with `ConfigFrom` responds
201 only when the config-only network exists on the manager that handles the request, whether or
not that manager runs tasks on the network. Each node that runs a task on the network uses its
own config-only network of that name. Task placement does not exclude nodes that do not have the
config-only network: when the only nodes that can take a service's task do not have it, the task
is placed on one of them and rejected. On such a node, when the network is attachable,
`POST /containers/{id}/start` for a created or stopped standalone container on the
network responds with a 4xx or 5xx status.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-ON-LEADER"></a>

A Swarm-scoped network whose driver or IPAM driver is a managed plugin is created and allocated
only while the leader manager has the plugin. After leadership moves to a manager without the
plugin, the network still reports its allocation. But the tasks that services on it get after

manager's log reports the failure.

`POST /networks/create` for a Swarm-scoped network whose network driver is a managed
plugin's name without its tag responds 500. With an IPAM driver that is a managed plugin's name
without its tag, the request responds 201, and the network is never allocated.

start. Under the default restart policy, such a task is replaced indefinitely.

<a id="swarm-networking-overlay-networks"></a>

### Overlay networks

The expectations in this subsection depend on the addresses that are allocated for a network: its
subnets, task addresses and VIPs. These addresses are allocated only for an overlay network. Where
an expectation says that `GET /services/{id}` then reports a VIP, it reports it within the
[*allocation ceiling (30 s)*](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION) after the request responds.

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST**: A subnet's VXLAN traffic carries the VNI at its position in vxlanid_list

*Observed from:* underlay · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-VNI-LIST](#REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-VNI-LIST) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION), [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

A user-specified `vxlanid_list` is honored: for each *n* at which the network has a
subnet and the list has a VNI, the VXLAN traffic of the network's *n*-th subnet, in the order of
the network's subnets, carries the *n*-th VNI of the list. On a Windows node, this holds for
VNIs of 4096 or more.

<a id="SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-SHORT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-SHORT**: A short vxlanid_list gets auto-allocated VNIs for the remaining subnets

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-VNI-LIST](#REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-VNI-LIST), [REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-VNI-REPORTED](#REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-VNI-REPORTED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION)

`POST /networks/create` for an overlay network whose `vxlanid_list` has fewer
VNIs than the network has subnets responds 201. Once the network is allocated, `GET /networks/{id}` on a manager reports the same number of VNIs in `vxlanid_list` as the
overlay has subnets. These are the requested VNIs, then an auto-allocated VNI for each remaining
subnet.

<a id="SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-LONG"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-LONG**: A long vxlanid_list gives the network its first VNIs

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-VNI-LIST](#REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-VNI-LIST), [REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-VNI-REPORTED](#REQ-SWARM-OVERLAY-VNI-REPORTED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-LONG-SURPLUS-DROPPED](#SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-LONG-SURPLUS-DROPPED)

`POST /networks/create` for an overlay network whose `vxlanid_list` has more
VNIs than the network has subnets responds 201. Once the network is allocated, `GET /networks/{id}` on a manager reports the same number of VNIs in `vxlanid_list` as the
overlay has subnets. These are the first VNIs of the requested list.

<a id="SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-LONG-SURPLUS-DROPPED"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-LONG-SURPLUS-DROPPED**: The surplus VNIs of a long vxlanid_list are dropped without an error

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-LONG](#SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-LONG) · *Violates:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED)

`POST /networks/create` for an overlay network whose `vxlanid_list` has more
VNIs than the network has subnets responds 201, and the VNIs beyond the number of subnets are
dropped. `GET /networks/{id}` does not report them. They are not reserved: `POST /networks/create` for another overlay network whose `vxlanid_list` has one of them
responds 201, and that network is then allocated.

<a id="SWARM-OVL-VNI-DUPLICATE"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-OVL-VNI-DUPLICATE**: An overlay network with another overlay's VNI is created without a warning

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*CLI form:* [SWARM-OVL-VNI-DUPLICATE-CLI](#SWARM-OVL-VNI-DUPLICATE-CLI) · *Pins:* [SWARM-OVL-ALLOCATION-FAILURE-UNREPORTED](#SWARM-OVL-ALLOCATION-FAILURE-UNREPORTED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-OVL-UNALLOCATED-LISTED](#SWARM-OVL-UNALLOCATED-LISTED), [SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-CTR-START](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-CTR-START) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-OVL-ALLOCATION-FAILURE-UNREPORTED](#SWARM-OVL-ALLOCATION-FAILURE-UNREPORTED) · *Violates:* [PRIN-WARN-AHEAD](../principles.md#PRIN-WARN-AHEAD), [REQ-SWARM-TASK-ERRORS](#REQ-SWARM-TASK-ERRORS)

*Applies to:* An allocated overlay network

`POST /networks/create` for another overlay network, with a VNI in its
`vxlanid_list` that `GET /networks/{id}` reports in the first network's
`vxlanid_list`, responds 201 without a warning about the VNI. `GET /networks` on
a manager then lists the new network. The new network is not allocated while the first network
exists, and the tasks of a service on the new network stay in the `new` state that
`GET /tasks` reports. Within the [*allocation ceiling (30 s)*](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION) after `DELETE /networks/{id}` for the first network responds,
the new network is allocated.

*Pinned by:* [SWARM-OVL-VNI-DUPLICATE](#SWARM-OVL-VNI-DUPLICATE), [SWARM-OVL-VNI-DUPLICATE-CLI](#SWARM-OVL-VNI-DUPLICATE-CLI), [SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-CREATE](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-CREATE), [SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-CREATE-CLI](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-CREATE-CLI), [SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-INSPECT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-INSPECT), [SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-LOG](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-LOG), [SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-SERVICE](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-SERVICE), [SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-SERVICE-LOG](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-SERVICE-LOG) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-OVL-UNALLOCATED-LISTED](#SWARM-OVL-UNALLOCATED-LISTED), [SWARM-OVL-UNALLOCATED-OTHERS-LISTED](#SWARM-OVL-UNALLOCATED-OTHERS-LISTED), [SWARM-OVL-VNI-DUPLICATE](#SWARM-OVL-VNI-DUPLICATE), [SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-CTR-START](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-CTR-START), [SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-ALLOCATED](#SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-ALLOCATED) · *Violates:* [PRIN-WARN-AHEAD](../principles.md#PRIN-WARN-AHEAD), [REQ-NET-INSPECT-CONFIGURATION](network-common.md#REQ-NET-INSPECT-CONFIGURATION), [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-SUBNET-CONFIG](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-SUBNET-CONFIG), [REQ-SWARM-TASK-ERRORS](#REQ-SWARM-TASK-ERRORS)

`POST /networks/create` for an overlay network that cannot be allocated responds 201.
This occurs when a VNI in the network's `vxlanid_list` is in use, or when its address
pool is exhausted. It also occurs when its requested subnet overlaps the subnet of another Swarm
network. It also occurs when it has an IPv6 subnet under the default IPAM driver. Networks are
allocated asynchronously. When a network cannot be allocated, the leader manager's log gets an
entry at the error level that contains `Failed allocation for network`, or `failed allocating network` for a network that a manager finds unallocated when it becomes leader, and
the network's ID. Once the network that holds what it needs is removed, the network is allocated
within the [*allocation ceiling (30 s)*](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION) after the
request that removes it responds. What it needs is the VNI in its `vxlanid_list`, a
subnet of its exhausted address pool, or the subnet that its requested subnet overlaps. A
network with an IPv6 subnet under the default IPAM driver is never allocated. The response to
the create has an empty `Warning`. `POST /services/create` for a service on
such a network also responds 201, without warnings. While the network is not allocated,
`GET /tasks` reports each of the service's tasks in the `new` state, without an error.
On a manager, `GET /networks/{id}` reports the network with an empty `Driver`
and `IPAM`, even when the request named them.

<a id="SWARM-OVL-MTU-ANY-VALUE-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-OVL-MTU-ANY-VALUE-CLI**: docker network create accepts and inspect prints any overlay mtu value

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux

*CLI form of:* [SWARM-OVL-MTU-ANY-VALUE](#SWARM-OVL-MTU-ANY-VALUE) · *Pins:* [SWARM-OVL-MTU-UNCHECKED](#SWARM-OVL-MTU-UNCHECKED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-OVL-MTU-UNCHECKED](#SWARM-OVL-MTU-UNCHECKED)

`docker network create --driver overlay` exits zero whatever value `--opt` gives
`com.docker.network.driver.mtu`. `docker network inspect` on a manager then prints
that value in the network's options.

<a id="SWARM-OVL-MTU-UNCHECKED"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-OVL-MTU-UNCHECKED**: mtu on overlay networks is not checked at create

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Pinned by:* [SWARM-OVL-MTU-ANY-VALUE](#SWARM-OVL-MTU-ANY-VALUE), [SWARM-OVL-MTU-ANY-VALUE-CLI](#SWARM-OVL-MTU-ANY-VALUE-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-OVL-MTU-ANY-VALUE](#SWARM-OVL-MTU-ANY-VALUE), [SWARM-OVL-MTU-ANY-VALUE-CLI](#SWARM-OVL-MTU-ANY-VALUE-CLI), [SWARM-OVLOPT-MTU](#SWARM-OVLOPT-MTU) · *Violates:* [PRIN-ERRORS-ACTIONABLE](../principles.md#PRIN-ERRORS-ACTIONABLE), [PRIN-FAIL-FAST](../principles.md#PRIN-FAIL-FAST)

`POST /networks/create` for an overlay network with any value of
`com.docker.network.driver.mtu` responds 201. If the value is not a non-negative
integer, a Linux node rejects all tasks on the network that are assigned to that node. Their
errors contain `failed to parse` or `invalid MTU value`. The
`failed to parse` error gives the value and does not name the option. If the kernel
cannot create the network's interfaces with the value, a Linux node also rejects every such
task.

<a id="SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES-CREATE"></a>

<a id="SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES**: A task or VIP gets an overlay's AuxiliaryAddresses when no other is free

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Pins:* [SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES-IGNORED](#SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES-IGNORED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES-CREATE](#SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES-CREATE) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES-IGNORED](#SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES-IGNORED) · *Violates:* [REQ-NET-INSPECT-CONFIGURATION](network-common.md#REQ-NET-INSPECT-CONFIGURATION)

*Applies to:* An overlay network created with `AuxiliaryAddresses` in
`IPAM.Config`

`GET /networks/{id}` on a manager does not report these addresses. When every other
address of the subnet is in use, a task or VIP that is then allocated on the network gets one of
these addresses.

<a id="SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES-IGNORED"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES-IGNORED**: AuxiliaryAddresses of an overlay are accepted and not reserved

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Pinned by:* [SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES](#SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES](#SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES), [SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES-CREATE](#SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES-CREATE) · *Violates:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED)

`POST /networks/create` accepts `AuxiliaryAddresses` in the
`IPAM.Config` of an overlay network, but they are not kept. These addresses are not
reserved: when every other address of the subnet is in use, a task or VIP that is then allocated
on the network gets one of them.

*Applies to:* A created or stopped container with a static IPv4 address on an attachable
overlay, and another container on the overlay that uses that address

`POST /containers/{id}/start` responds 500 after 20 seconds. The response's message
contains `attaching to network failed, make sure your network options are correct and check manager logs: context deadline exceeded`.

*Refines:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED), [REQ-SWARM-ATTACH-FAILURE-START](#REQ-SWARM-ATTACH-FAILURE-START), [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-STATIC-ADDRESS](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-STATIC-ADDRESS) · *CLI form of:* [SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE](#SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-OUTSIDE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

exits with status 125 and prints the daemon's error.

<a id="SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-RELEASED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-RELEASED**: A container's address is free for a static address once it leaves

*Observed from:* api:mgr, api:active · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [PRIN-NO-LEAKS](../principles.md#PRIN-NO-LEAKS), [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-ATTACHMENT-RELEASED](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-ATTACHMENT-RELEASED), [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-STATIC-ADDRESS](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-STATIC-ADDRESS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

*Applies to:* A standalone container on an attachable overlay

After the container disconnects from the overlay or stops, its attachment task disappears from
`GET /tasks` on a manager. On any node whose availability is `active`, `POST /containers/{id}/start` for another container on the overlay, with the first container's address
as its static IPv4 address, then responds 204.

`GET /services/{id}` reports one VIP in `Endpoint.VirtualIPs` for each
overlay network that the service is attached to. Each of these VIPs is in one of that network's

<a id="SWARM-OVL-V6-ADDRESSING"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-OVL-V6-ADDRESSING**: An overlay with an IPv6 subnet is accepted and never allocated

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Pinned by:* [SWARM-HOSTPUB-CLIENT-SOURCE-V6](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-HOSTPUB-CLIENT-SOURCE-V6), [SWARM-PUB-V6-NO-USERLAND-PROXY](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-PUB-V6-NO-USERLAND-PROXY) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-CTR-ADDRESS](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-CTR-ADDRESS), [SWARM-OVL-VIP-PER-NETWORK](#SWARM-OVL-VIP-PER-NETWORK) · *Violates:* [PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED](../principles.md#PRIN-FAILS-CLOSED), [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-SUBNET-CONFIG](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-SUBNET-CONFIG)

With the default IPAM driver, `POST /networks/create` accepts an overlay network with an
IPv6 subnet, but the network is never allocated. An overlay network with `EnableIPv6`
set and without an IPv6 subnet is accepted, and the network's attachments get IPv4 addresses
only. Each attachment gets exactly one address.

The VIP that `GET /networks/{id}?verbose=true` reports for a service is the address that
load-balances to its tasks.

<a id="SWARM-OVL-VERBOSE-TASKS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-OVL-VERBOSE-TASKS**: Verbose network inspect lists running tasks and no stopped task

*Observed from:* api:mgr, api:wkr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-VERBOSE-INSPECT](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-VERBOSE-INSPECT) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION), [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

*Applies to:* A node with a local attachment to an overlay network, and a service on that
network

Within the [*reassignment ceiling (300 s)*](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) after a
task of the service is added, and within the [*allocation ceiling (30 s)*](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION) after a task's container exits or its desired state changes from
`running`, the tasks that `GET /networks/{id}?verbose=true` reports for the service
include each of its running tasks, as [Service discovery](swarm-traffic.md#swarm-traffic-service-discovery) in
[swarm-traffic.md](swarm-traffic.md) defines them. They do not include a task whose container
has stopped.

<a id="SWARM-OVL-VERBOSE-SERVICES"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-OVL-VERBOSE-SERVICES**: Verbose network inspect on an attached node reports Services

*Observed from:* api:mgr, api:wkr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-VERBOSE-INSPECT](#REQ-SWARM-NETWORK-VERBOSE-INSPECT) · *CLI form:* [SWARM-OVL-VERBOSE-SERVICES-CLI](#SWARM-OVL-VERBOSE-SERVICES-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

`Services`. `Services` gives the VIP of each service and the endpoint IP

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Rationale:* Some fields of a Swarm-scoped network describe the node that answers, not the cluster ([RAT-SWARM-NODE-REPORTS-OWN-STATE](#RAT-SWARM-NODE-REPORTS-OWN-STATE))

<a id="swarm-networking-the-ingress-network"></a>

### The ingress network

A Swarm-scoped network created with `Ingress` set is an ingress network. A Swarm-scoped
network named `ingress` and created with the label `com.docker.swarm.internal` in
`Labels` is also an ingress network, whatever its driver and the label's value. Older
daemons created the ingress network in this second form, without `Ingress`. `GET /networks` reports `Ingress` as true for both forms.

An ingress network exists while `GET /networks` on a manager lists a network whose
`Ingress` is true. That network is the ingress network. `docker swarm init` creates
it with `Ingress` set and names it `ingress`. It can be removed, and an ingress
network can then be created with another name. A copy that a node keeps after the network is deleted
([*SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-DELETE-STALE*](#SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-DELETE-STALE)) does not count. Nor does a network created in the second
form while another ingress network exists, which is never allocated
([*SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-SECOND*](#SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-SECOND)).

The managers give every node of the Swarm an address on the ingress network for the node's
load-balancer endpoint. A node that has such an address on an ingress network created with
`Ingress` set creates the network and its load-balancer endpoint on it, whether or not a
task runs on the node, and so has a local attachment to the network. When the network is deleted,
the node removes it and has no local attachment to it. A node does not create an ingress network of
the second form for its address on it. It has a local attachment to such a network only once a task
on the node of a service that publishes a port in ingress mode, or a standalone container on the
node, attaches to the network.

<a id="SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-NODE-LOCAL-DRIVER"></a>

**Expectation (defect) SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-NODE-LOCAL-DRIVER**: A node-local labeled ingress is created and its tasks are rejected

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-INGRESS-NODE-LOCAL-DRIVER](#SWARM-INGRESS-NODE-LOCAL-DRIVER) · *Violates:* [REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-OVERLAY-ONLY](#REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-OVERLAY-ONLY)

*Applies to:* A Swarm without an ingress network

On a manager, `POST /networks/create` for a Swarm-scoped network of a node-local driver,
named `ingress`, with the label `com.docker.swarm.internal` and without
`Ingress`, responds 201. `GET /networks` on a manager then lists it with
`Ingress` true. The tasks of a service that publishes a port in ingress mode are then
rejected, and their error in `GET /tasks` contains `Ingress network can only be global scope network`.

<a id="SWARM-INGRESS-DELETE-DECLINED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) SWARM-INGRESS-DELETE-DECLINED**: docker network rm for ingress warns, asks [y/N], and keeps the network when declined

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-REMOVE-CONFIRM](#REQ-SWARM-INGRESS-REMOVE-CONFIRM) · *Exact form:* [SWARM-INGRESS-DELETE-DECLINED-EXIT-ZERO](#SWARM-INGRESS-DELETE-DECLINED-EXIT-ZERO) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A Swarm with an ingress network

removes the network. Given an answer other than `y` or `Y` at that prompt, it does not
remove the network: `docker network ls` then still lists it.

*Pins:* [SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-PARTLY-SUPPORTED](#SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-PARTLY-SUPPORTED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Concerns:* [SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-DELETE-STALE](#SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-DELETE-STALE) · *Concerned by:* [SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-PARTLY-SUPPORTED](#SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-PARTLY-SUPPORTED) · *Violates:* [PRIN-ERRORS-ACTIONABLE](../principles.md#PRIN-ERRORS-ACTIONABLE)

*Applies to:* A Swarm with a node that has a local attachment to an overlay network named
`ingress` created with the label `com.docker.swarm.internal` and without
`Ingress`, where no service publishes a port in ingress mode

`DELETE /networks/{id}` for that network responds 204. Before the node's daemon
restarts, tasks on that node that attach to a new ingress network with an overlapping subnet are
rejected. Their error in `GET /tasks` contains `invalid pool request`. The
error says `Pool overlaps with other one on this address space`. It names neither the
subnet nor the deleted network whose copy holds it.

`POST /networks/create` for an overlay network named `ingress` with the label
`com.docker.swarm.internal` and without `Ingress` responds 201, also with
`Attachable` true, and also while an ingress network with another name exists, in
which case the network is never allocated. A port that a service publishes in ingress mode
through such a network answers at the address of a node only while that node has a local
attachment to the network. After `DELETE /networks/{id}` for the network, each node that
had a local attachment to it keeps its copy until its daemon restarts, and until then the tasks
on that node that attach to a new ingress network whose subnet overlaps it are rejected.

<a id="swarm-networking-deliberately-not-asserted"></a>

## Deliberately not asserted

These items are incidental to the implementation. A change to any of them does not break any
expectation.

- The counters of Moby's own rules.
- Precedence over an operator's rule that the operator inserts at the top of the filter table's
  `INPUT` chain after an `encrypted` network is programmed. Such a rule can
  accept cleartext VXLAN for the network's VNI ([*SWARM-IPT-ENCRYPTED-INPUT-ACCEPT*](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-IPT-ENCRYPTED-INPUT-ACCEPT) covers a
  rule at the end of the chain).
- The content of Moby's own chains and tables, and their names other than `DOCKER-USER`,
  except where [Cross-generation cleanup](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-cross-generation-cleanup) in [swarm-lifecycle.md](swarm-lifecycle.md) pins them for cleanup and [Rule content](bridge-networking.md#bridge-networking-rule-content) in
  [bridge-networking.md](bridge-networking.md) pins the bridge driver's rules.
  [*SWARM-NFT-REFERENCE*](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-NFT-REFERENCE) also asserts the content of the overlay driver's nftables table. The
  content includes individual match/target lines and their order in a chain. A backend change
  replaces exactly these rules. A contract asserts their effect on packets, and never the content.
  This item does not include the overlay driver's base-chain hooks and priorities.
  [*SWARM-NFT-OVERLAY-TABLE*](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-NFT-OVERLAY-TABLE) asserts them.
- Which packet-filtering technology is in use, beyond what the expectations of
  [Firewall anchors & host integration](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-firewall-anchors-host-integration) in [swarm-lifecycle.md](swarm-lifecycle.md) about anchors, cleanup and the overlay driver's nftables table assert for each
  backend.
- The existence, name or topology of internal sandboxes (per-network load-balancer sandbox, ingress
  sandbox), network-namespace paths, and generated `veth` / bridge / VXLAN interface
  names. One exception is the name `ingress-sbox` in `Containers` of `GET /networks/docker_gwbridge`, which [*NET-API-GWBRIDGE-INGRESS-SBOX*](network-common.md#NET-API-GWBRIDGE-INGRESS-SBOX) asserts. Another exception
  is a node's load-balancer endpoint on a network. `GET /networks/{id}` on that node lists
  this endpoint. [*SWARM-OVL-IPRANGE*](#SWARM-OVL-IPRANGE) asserts where its address falls, and
  [*SWARM-LB-NAT-SOURCE-LB-ADDRESS*](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-LB-NAT-SOURCE-LB-ADDRESS) asserts that a task observes it as the source address in
  NAT mode. The key and the name of this endpoint are not asserted.
  [*NET-RESTART-NAMESPACES-REMOVED*](network-common.md#NET-RESTART-NAMESPACES-REMOVED) asserts that the namespaces of these sandboxes are removed
  after a kill and restart.
- The load-balancer implementation and its scheduler, beyond the distribution property in
  [Distribution](swarm-traffic.md#swarm-traffic-distribution) in [swarm-traffic.md](swarm-traffic.md).
- Internal refcounting, gossip timers, and reap and rejoin intervals. The surface for these is the
  convergence bounds in [Convergence](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-convergence) in [swarm-lifecycle.md](swarm-lifecycle.md).
- The order in which the daemon allocates subnets from an address pool, addresses within a subnet,
  published ports from the auto-assignment range, and VNIs to networks created without
  `vxlanid_list`. Of the addresses within a subnet, [*SWARM-OVL-IPRANGE-GATEWAY*](#SWARM-OVL-IPRANGE-GATEWAY)
  asserts which address is the gateway of a subnet with an `IPRange`.
- The value of `LocalLBIndex`. `docker network inspect --verbose` shows this value,
  but the value is an internal firewall mark.
- The host-port reservation mechanics behind [Port allocation](swarm-traffic.md#swarm-traffic-port-allocation) in
  [swarm-traffic.md](swarm-traffic.md).
- Whether Windows nodes can use a VNI below 4096.
